extraction_notes.note: The enumerated items of the proof of Lemma 4.2 are labelled and cited later as 'Claims'; items 1 and 3-6 are emitted as Level-1 claims nested in the proof, the uncited items 2, 7, 8 as proof steps. Item 5 is mostly an application of Lemma 9.4 but is cited as a claim.

Subsection 9.2.4 is a derivation that (58) implies (57), justifying a sentence inside the proof of the claim on large normal components; no separately stated result exists, so it is a remark linked to that proof.
The proof of Lemma 10.24 cites 'Lemma B.6', a stale appendix number; the bound used matches the Bounding Ball lemma (Lemma 8.6), linked with an inferred low-confidence edge.
Remarks 8.1 and 8.2 state standard Taylor inequalities; kept as remarks (author's word) with origin external, rather than claims.

Motivational and road-map paragraphs (bias discussion in Section 2.2.2, 'Back to Theorem 3.3 proof road-map', conclusions/future directions) and the two omitted tikz road-map figures were not extracted.

The 'Idea of the proof' of Lemma 4.1 is a proof sketch; the prompt asks for rigor semi_formal on a sketch while the finishing step says rigor never goes on proofs. Kept semi_formal, as the sketch rule is more specific.

nodes.name: Reach
nodes.statement: The reach of a subset $A$ of $\mathbb{R}^D$, is the largest $\tau$ \emph{(}possibly $\infty$\emph{)} such that for any $x\in\mathbb{R}^D$ that maintains $dist(A,x)\leq \tau$, there exists a unique point $Proj_A(x)\in A$, nearest to $x$.
nodes.statement_short: The reach of $A$ is the largest $\tau$ such that every point within distance $\tau$ of $A$ has a unique nearest point in $A$.
nodes.label: def:reach

nodes.name: Uniform tubular noise model
nodes.statement_short: Samples $r_i$ are drawn i.i.d. uniformly from the $\sigma$-tubular neighborhood $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ of $\mathcal{M}$.

nodes.name: Tubular neighborhood M_sigma
nodes.statement:
\mathcal{M}_\sigma \stackrel{\bigtriangleup}{=} \{q\in \mathbb{R}^D ~|~ dist(q, \mathcal{M}) < \sigma \}
	,
nodes.label: eq:Msigma

nodes.name: Local chart phi_p over the tangent space
nodes.statement_short: Locally $\mathcal{M}$ near $p$ is the graph $\varphi_p(x)=p+(x,\phi_p(x))$ of a function from the tangent space to its orthogonal complement.

nodes.name: Local chart map varphi_p
nodes.statement: \varphi_p:W_{T_p\mathcal{M}}\to \mathcal{M}
nodes.label: eq:LocalChart_clean

nodes.name: Definition of varphi_p via phi_p
nodes.statement: \varphi_p(x) = p+(x,\phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}} ,
nodes.label: eq:phi_def_clean

nodes.name: Graph of phi_p
Graph Gamma_{phi_p,W_p}
nodes.statement:
\Gamma_{\phi_p, W_p} \stackrel{\bigtriangleup}{=} \{p + (x, \phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}} | x\in W_{T_p\mathcal{M}} \}  
	.
nodes.label: eq:FunctionGraph_init

nodes.name: Compact C^k submanifold without boundary
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{M}\in\mathcal{C}^k$ is a compact $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ without boundary
nodes.section: 2.1 Summary of manifold and sampling assumptions
also_stated_at: $\mathcal{M}\in\mathcal{C}^k$ is a compact $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ without boundary.

nodes.name: Reach-to-noise ratio M large enough
nodes.statement: $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$ is large enough, where $\tau$ is the reach of $\mathcal{M}$ and $\sigma>0$ is the noise level.
nodes.section: 2.1 Summary of manifold and sampling assumptions
also_stated_at: $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$ is large enough, where $\tau$ is the reach of $\mathcal{M}$ and $\sigma>0$ is the noise level.
nodes.statement_short: The ratio $M=\tau/\sigma$ of reach to noise level is assumed large enough.

nodes.name: I.i.d. uniform sampling from M_sigma
nodes.statement: $\{r_i\}_{i=1}^n$ are samples drawn independently and uniformly from $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ (i.e., $r_i\sim \operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal{M}_\sigma)$).
nodes.section: 2.1 Summary of manifold and sampling assumptions
also_stated_at: $\{r_i\}_{i=1}^n$ are samples drawn independently and uniformly from $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ (that is, $r_i\sim \operatorname{Unif}(\mathcal{M}_\sigma)$).

nodes.name: Region of interest U_ROI
nodes.statement_short: The ROI is the set of samples within distance $\sqrt{\sigma\tau}$ of $r$; $N$ is its size.

nodes.name: ROI definition
nodes.statement:
U_{\textrm{ROI}} = {\{r_i|\operatorname{dist}(r_i,r)<\sqrt{\sigma\tau}\}}
	,
nodes.label: eq:ROI_clean

nodes.name: Step 1 constrained minimization of J_1
nodes.statement_short: Find an affine coordinate system $(q,H)$ minimizing the mean squared distance $J_1$ of ROI samples to $q+H$, with $r-q\perp H$ and $\|r-q\|<2\sigma$.

nodes.name: Functional J_1
nodes.statement: J_1(r; q, H) = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{r_i\in U_{\textrm{ROI}}} \operatorname{dist}^2 (r_i - q,H)
nodes.label: eq:J1_clean

nodes.name: Minimizer (q*, H*) of J_1
nodes.statement: q^*(r), H^*(r) = \arg\!\min_{\substack{ q, H \\ r-q \perp H \\ \|r- q\|<2\sigma}} J_1(r; q, H)
nodes.label: eq:argmin1_clean

nodes.name: Algorithm 1: Find an initial coordinate system
nodes.statement_short: Restrict the samples to the ROI and solve the constrained minimization of $J_1$ for an initial point $q^*$ and tangent estimate $H^*$.
input: $\{r_i\}_{i=1}^n\subset \mathcal{M}_\sigma$ & noisy samples of a $d$ dimensional manifold $ \mathcal{M} $.
$r\in \mathcal{M}_\sigma$ & a point in a tubular neighborhood of $\mathcal{M}$.
nodes.label: alg:alg1_clean

nodes.name: Restrict to the ROI
nodes.statement: Disregard points outside of $U_{\textrm{ROI}}$ (plugging $\tau_\text{bound}, \sigma_\text{bound}$ into Eq. \eqref{eq:ROI_clean}).

nodes.name: Minimize J_1 under constraints
nodes.statement: Find $q^*, H^*$ minimizing \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean} subject to $\norm{q^* - r}<2\sigma$ and $r - q^* \perp H^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Solve the constrained minimization of $J_1$ for $(q^*,H^*)$.

nodes.name: Local polynomial regression
nodes.statement_short: Fit a degree-$(k-1)$ polynomial $\pi$ over $H$ to the ROI samples within bandwidth $\epsilon_n$ by least squares ($J_2$).

nodes.name: Functional J_2
nodes.statement:
J_2(\pi ~|~ q, H) = \frac{1}{N_{q, H}}\sum_{r_i \in U_{\textrm{ROI}}^n} \norm{r_i - (x_i, \pi(x_i))_H}^2
	,
nodes.label: eq:Step2_clean

nodes.name: Bandwidth-restricted ROI U^n_ROI(q,H)
nodes.statement:
U_{\textrm{ROI}}^n(q,H) = {\{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}~|~\norm{x_i}<\epsilon_n\}}
	,
nodes.label: eq:ROI_ell_clean

nodes.name: Local polynomial regression minimizer pi*
nodes.statement:
\pi^*_{q, H} = \arg\!\min_{\pi\in \Pi_{k-1}^{d\mapsto D}} J_2(\pi ~|~ q, H)
	.
nodes.label: eq:argmin2_clean

nodes.name: Bandwidth decay rate
nodes.statement_short: The bandwidth $\epsilon_n\to0$ at rate $n^{-1/(2k+d)}$.

nodes.name: Bandwidth decay condition
nodes.statement:
0<\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty}n^{1/(2k+d)}\cdot \epsilon_n < \infty
	.
nodes.label: eq:bandwidthDecay_clean

nodes.name: Median-trick estimator pi*
nodes.statement:
For simplicity of notations, we abuse the definition of $ \pi^*_{q, H}$ in \eqref{eq:argmin2_clean}, and define
\begin{equation} \pi^*_{q, H} = \mbox{Algorithm 2 of \cite{aizenbud2021VectorEstimation}} (x_i,y_i),
\end{equation}
where $y_i$ are the projection of $r_i-q$ onto $H^\perp$.
nodes.statement_short: $\pi^*_{q,H}$ is redefined as the output of the median-trick variant (Algorithm 2 of Aizenbud et al.) of local polynomial regression.

nodes.name: pi* via Algorithm 2 of Aizenbud et al.
nodes.statement: \pi^*_{q, H} = \mbox{Algorithm 2 of \cite{aizenbud2021VectorEstimation}} (x_i,y_i),
nodes.label: eq:pi_star_median_trick

nodes.name: Derivative notation for pi*
nodes.statement: For simplicity of presentation, throughout the paper when we write $\partial \pi^*_{q, H}$ or $\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}}$ what we actually mean is the estimate of the derivative rather than the derivative of $\pi^*_{q, H}$.

nodes.name: Updated tangent estimate H_{l+1}
nodes.statement: Explicitly, in iteration $\ell$, we define $H_{\ell+1}$ to be the subspace coinciding with $ \mathrm{Im}(\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{r, H_{\ell}}}[0]) $ the image of the differential of $(\textrm{I}_d,\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}):\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^D$ at $ 0 $ (i.e., the tangent to the graph of $ \pi^*_{r, H_{\ell }} $).
nodes.statement_short: $H_{\ell+1}$ is the image of the differential at 0 of the graph map of the fitted polynomial $\pi^*_{r,H_\ell}$.

nodes.name: Local function f_l over H_l
f_l : H_l -> H_l^perp
nodes.statement:
f_{\ell}:\mathbb{R}^d\simeq H_\ell \to \mathbb{R}^{D-d} \simeq H_\ell ^\perp 
	.

nodes.name: Local patch Gamma_{f_l,r,H_l}
nodes.statement:
That is, we define a local patch of the manifold through the graph 
\begin{equation} \Gamma_{f_\ell, r, H_\ell} = \{r + (x, f_\ell(x))_{H_\ell} | x\in B_{H_\ell}(0,\rho) \}\subset\mathcal{M},   
\end{equation}
where $\rho$ is some radius where this function is defined (see Lemma \ref{lem:M_is_locally_a_fuinction_clean} for more details regarding the existence of such $\rho > 0$).

nodes.name: Graph of f_l
nodes.statement: \Gamma_{f_\ell, r, H_\ell} = \{r + (x, f_\ell(x))_{H_\ell} | x\in B_{H_\ell}(0,\rho) \}\subset\mathcal{M},
nodes.label: eq:Graph_fl

nodes.name: Next local function f_{l+1}
f_{l+1} over (r, H_{l+1})
nodes.statement: f_{\ell+1}:(r, H_{\ell+1}) \to H_{\ell+1} ^\perp \simeq \mathbb{R}^{D-d}
nodes.label: eq:fl_def

nodes.name: Final estimates hat p_n and tangent
nodes.statement_short: After $\kappa$ iterations, $\hat p_n$ is the fitted polynomial's value at 0 over $(r,H_\kappa)$ and the tangent estimate is $H_\kappa$.

nodes.name: Estimates hat p_n and hat T
nodes.statement:
\hat p_n \stackrel{\bigtriangleup}{=} (0, \pi^*_{r, H_\kappa}(0))_{r, H_\kappa} ,\quad \widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}} \stackrel{\bigtriangleup}{=} H_\kappa
	.

nodes.name: Algorithm 2: Iterated projection (Step 2)
nodes.statement_short: Iteratively refit a local polynomial over the current tangent estimate and replace the tangent by the fitted polynomial's tangent at 0; output the fitted point and tangent.
input: $\{r_i\}_{i=1}^n\subset \mathcal{M}_\sigma$ & Noisy samples of a $d$ dimensional manifold $ \mathcal{M} $.
nodes.label: alg:step2_clean

nodes.name: Loop over kappa iterations
nodes.statement:
\For{$\ell=0$ to $\kappa-1$}
		\State Compute  $\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}$ through a version of linear least-squares minimization  \eqref{eq:pi_star_median_trick}.
		\State Compute $ \mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}}[0] $ the differential of  $\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}$ in some basis at zero.
		\State $H_{\ell+1} = \mathrm{Im}(\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}}[0]) $ \Comment{this is the column space of $ \mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}}[0] $}.

nodes.name: Fit local polynomial
nodes.statement: Compute  $\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}$ through a version of linear least-squares minimization  \eqref{eq:pi_star_median_trick}.
nodes.statement_short: Fit $\pi^*_{r,H_\ell}$ by the median-trick least squares.

nodes.name: Differential at zero
nodes.statement: Compute $ \mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}}[0] $ the differential of  $\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}$ in some basis at zero.

nodes.name: Update tangent H_{l+1}
nodes.statement: $H_{\ell+1} = \mathrm{Im}(\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}}[0]) $ \Comment{this is the column space of $ \mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{r,H_{\ell}}}[0] $}.
nodes.statement_short: Set the new tangent estimate to the column space of the differential.

nodes.name: Tangent estimate
nodes.statement: $\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}} = H_\kappa $

nodes.name: Return estimates
nodes.statement: \Return $\hat p_n$ and $\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}}$.

nodes.name: Convergence of Algorithm 3 to a local minimizer
nodes.statement: Algorithm \ref{alg:step1Inpractice_clean} can be shown to converge in theory to a local minimizer of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean}.
conclusions: Algorithm \ref{alg:step1Inpractice_clean} can be shown to converge in theory to a local minimizer of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean}

nodes.name: Algorithm 3: Step 1 in practice
nodes.statement_short: Alternating scheme: start from local PCA, then repeatedly fit an affine least-squares model over the current basis, re-orthonormalize via QR and re-project $q$, until $q$ stabilizes.
output: $U$ - an $n\times d$ matrix whose columns are $\lbrace u_j \rbrace_{j=1}^d$
nodes.label: alg:step1Inpractice_clean

nodes.name: Data matrix R
nodes.statement: define $R$ to be an $n\times N$ matrix whose columns are $r_i$

nodes.name: Initialize U with weighted PCA
nodes.statement: initialize $U$ with the first $d$ principal components of the spatially weighted PCA
nodes.statement_short: Initialize the basis with the top $d$ spatially weighted principal components.
nodes.label: algstep:U_init_in_practice

nodes.name: Initialize q
nodes.statement: $q\leftarrow r$

nodes.name: Repeat until convergence
Store previous q
nodes.statement: $q_{prev} = q$

nodes.name: Centered ROI samples
nodes.statement: $\tilde{R} = (R - repmat(q,1,N))\cdot \Theta$ \Comment{where $\Theta$ is an indicator for points in $U_{\textrm{ROI}}$}
nodes.statement_short: Center the samples at $q$ and mask points outside the ROI.

nodes.name: Coordinates in Col(U)
nodes.statement: $X_{N\times d} = \tilde{R}^T U$ \Comment{find the representation of $r_i$ in $Col(U)$}

nodes.name: Augmented design matrix
nodes.statement: define $\tilde{X}_{N\times (d+1)} = \left[(1,...,1)^T, X\right]$

nodes.name: Least-squares fit
nodes.statement: solve $\tilde{X}^T\tilde{X}\alpha = \tilde{X}^T \tilde{R}^T$ for $\alpha \in M_{(d+1)\times n}$ \Comment{solving the LS minimization of $\tilde{X}\alpha \approx \tilde{R}^T$}
nodes.statement_short: Solve the normal equations of the affine least-squares fit.

nodes.name: Shifted origin
nodes.statement: $\tilde{q} = q + \alpha(1,:)^T$

nodes.name: QR decomposition
nodes.statement: $Q, \hat{R} = qr(\alpha(2:end, :)^T)$ \Comment{where $qr$ denotes the QR decomposition}

nodes.name: Update basis
nodes.statement: $U \leftarrow Q$

nodes.name: Re-project q
nodes.statement: $q = \tilde{q} + U U^T (r-\tilde{q})$
nodes.statement_short: Move $q$ so that $r-q$ is orthogonal to the new subspace.

nodes.name: Convergence test
nodes.statement: \Until {$\|q-q_{\text{prev}}\|<\epsilon$}

nodes.name: Algorithm 4: Step 2 in practice
nodes.statement:
\caption{Step 2: in practice} \begin{algorithmic}[1]
		\State {\bfseries Input:}\begin{tabular}[t]{ll}
            $\{r_i\}_{i=1}^n$& a set of points in $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ \\
            $d$ & The dimension of the manifold $\mathcal{M}$.\\
            $q_{-1}$ & a crude approximation of $p_r = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$ \\ &(initialized with $q^*$ of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean})\\
			
			$H_0$ & Initial approximation of $T_{p}\mathcal{M}$ s.t. $\angle_{\max}(H_0,T_{p}\mathcal{M}) < \alpha_0$ \\
            &(initialized with $H^*$ of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean})\\
			
		\end{tabular}
		\State {\bfseries Output:}\begin{tabular}[t]{ll}
				$\hat p_n$ & Estimation of some $p\in\mathcal{M}$.\\
				$\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}}$ & Estimate of  $T_p\mathcal{M}$.\\
		\end{tabular}
		
		\State Compute $\pi^*_{q_{-1}, H_0}$
		\State $q_0 = q_{-1} + (0,\pi^*_{q_{-1}, H_0}(0))_{H_0}$ 
        \Repeat 
        \State Compute $\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}$ through the least-squares minimization of \eqref{eq:argmin2_clean}.
        \State Compute $\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}}[0]$.
        \State Set $H_{\ell + 1} = \mathrm{Im}(\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}}[0])$
        \State Set $q_{\ell+1} = q_\ell + (0, \pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}(0))_{H_\ell}$
		\Until {$|q_{\ell} - q_{\ell +1}| \leq \epsilon$}
		\State \Return $\hat p_n = q_{\ell+1}$,  $\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}} = H_{\ell+1} $
		
	\end{algorithmic}
nodes.statement_short: Iterate local polynomial fits, updating both the origin $q_\ell$ and the tangent $H_\ell$ until the origin stops moving.
nodes.label: alg:step2InPractice_clean

nodes.name: Initial polynomial fit
nodes.statement: Compute $\pi^*_{q_{-1}, H_0}$

nodes.name: Repeat until convergence
nodes.statement:
\Repeat 
        \State Compute $\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}$ through the least-squares minimization of \eqref{eq:argmin2_clean}.
        \State Compute $\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}}[0]$.
        \State Set $H_{\ell + 1} = \mathrm{Im}(\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}}[0])$
        \State Set $q_{\ell+1} = q_\ell + (0, \pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}(0))_{H_\ell}$

nodes.name: Fit local polynomial
nodes.statement: Compute $\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}$ through the least-squares minimization of \eqref{eq:argmin2_clean}.

nodes.name: Differential at zero
nodes.statement: Compute $\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}}[0]$.

nodes.name: Update tangent
nodes.statement: Set $H_{\ell + 1} = \mathrm{Im}(\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}}[0])$

nodes.name: Update origin
nodes.statement: Set $q_{\ell+1} = q_\ell + (0, \pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}(0))_{H_\ell}$

nodes.name: Convergence test
nodes.statement: \Until {$|q_{\ell} - q_{\ell +1}| \leq \epsilon$}

nodes.name: Return estimates
nodes.statement: \Return $\hat p_n = q_{\ell+1}$,  $\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}} = H_{\ell+1} $

nodes.name: Main result: convergence rates of the two-step estimator
nodes.statement:
Assume $M > C_\tau \sqrt{D\log D}$ for some constant $C_\tau$ independent of $\tau$, and let $r\in \mathcal{M}_\sigma$.
	Then, for any $\delta>0$ arbitrarily small, there exists $ N $ such that for any number of samples $ n > N $,
	applying Algorithm~\ref{alg:step2_clean} with inputs $q_{-1}, H_0$ being the outputs of Algorithm~\ref{alg:alg1_clean}, and with the number of iterations $\kappa$ specified in Lemma \ref{lem:comute_kappa} and is dependent on $n,d, \delta, k$, we get $ \hat p_n, \widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}} $, for which 
	\[
	dist(\hat p_n, \mathcal{M}) \leq \frac{C_1\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}{n^{r_0}}
	\]
	\[
	\norm{\hat p_n - \mathbf{p}} \leq C_2\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) \left(\frac{ n}{\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)^2}\right)^{-r_1} = \wtilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{-r_1}) = \mathcal{O}(n^{-r_1})
	,\]
	and 
	\[
	\angle_{\max}(\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}},T_{\mathbf{p}}\mathcal{M}) \leq  C_3\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) \left(\frac{ n}{\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)^2}\right)^{-r_1} = \wtilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{-r_1}) 
	\]
	with probability of at least $ 1 - \delta $, where $ r_0 = \frac{k}{2k +d} $, $ r_1 = \frac{k-1}{2k +d} $ and $\mathbf{p} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}} (r)$ is the projection of $r$ onto $\mathcal{M}$.
assumptions: Assume $M > C_\tau \sqrt{D\log D}$ for some constant $C_\tau$ independent of $\tau$, and let $r\in \mathcal{M}_\sigma$.

applying Algorithm~\ref{alg:step2_clean} with inputs $q_{-1}, H_0$ being the outputs of Algorithm~\ref{alg:alg1_clean}, and with the number of iterations $\kappa$ specified in Lemma \ref{lem:comute_kappa}
conclusions: with probability of at least $ 1 - \delta $, where $ r_0 = \frac{k}{2k +d} $, $ r_1 = \frac{k-1}{2k +d} $ and $\mathbf{p} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}} (r)$ is the projection of $r$ onto $\mathcal{M}$.
nodes.statement_short: With high probability, $\hat p_n$ is $O(n^{-k/(2k+d)})$-close to $\mathcal{M}$, and $\hat p_n$ and its tangent are $\tilde O(n^{-(k-1)/(2k+d)})$-close to $Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$ and its tangent.
nodes.label: thm:MainResult

nodes.name: Number of iterations is logarithmic in n
nodes.statement: While the explicit formula for $\kappa$, the number of iterations needed in Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean}, is given in Lemma \ref{lem:comute_kappa}, it is worth mentioning that it depends only logarithmically on the number of samples $n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.1
nodes.statement: We derive the result of Theorem \ref{thm:MainResult} by showing that Algorithm \ref{alg:alg1_clean} yields a ``reasonable" estimation for the tangent directions (Theorem \ref{thm:Step1}), and the fact that Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean} yields estimates that converge to a point and its tangent on the original manifold as $n \to \infty$ (Theorem \ref{thm:Step2}). Consequently, Theorem \ref{thm:MainResult} can be proven directly from Theorems \ref{thm:Step1} and \ref{thm:Step2}.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Theorem 3.2 (Algorithm 1 gives a reasonable tangent) with Theorem 3.3 (Algorithm 2 converges from such an initialization).

nodes.name: Step 1 yields a coarse tangent estimate
nodes.statement:
Let $ (q^*(r), H^*(r)) $, the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:alg1_clean}, and let $p = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(q^*)$. 
	Denote $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$ for some constant $C_{M}$ (independent of $\alpha$ and $M$).
	Then, for any $\delta>0$ arbitrarily small, there exists $ N_{\delta} $ such that for all $ n > N_{\delta} $ 
	\[\angle_{\max}(H^*, T_p\mathcal{M})\leq \alpha\]
	with probability of at least $ 1 - \delta $.
	Furthermore, we have
	\[
	\norm{p - q^*} \leq 3 \sigma
	\]
assumptions: Let $ (q^*(r), H^*(r)) $, the output of Algorithm \ref{alg:alg1_clean}, and let $p = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(q^*)$.
Denote $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$ for some constant $C_{M}$ (independent of $\alpha$ and $M$).
nodes.statement_short: With high probability the Step 1 output $H^*$ is within angle $\sqrt{C_M/M}$ of the tangent at $Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(q^*)$, and $q^*$ is $3\sigma$-close to it.
nodes.label: thm:Step1

nodes.name: Step 2 converges to the projection and its tangent
nodes.statement:
Assume that $M>C_\tau\sqrt{D\log D}$.  Denote $\mathbf{p} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}} (r)$ where r is the input point for Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean}.
	Let $(q, H)$ be an initial coordinate system for which $\norm{q - p}\leq 3 \sigma$ and $ \angle_{\max} (H, T_p\mathcal{M}) \leq \sqrt{c_{M}/M}$, where $p= Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(q) \in \mathcal{M}$.
	For any $\delta>0$ arbitrarily small, denote by $ \hat p_n, \widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}} $ the estimates derived from Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean} initialized with $(q,H)$ with the number of iterations $\kappa$ specified in Lemma \ref{lem:comute_kappa}. Then, there is $ N_{\delta} $ such that for all $ n > N_{\delta}  $ we have 
	\begin{equation} dist(\hat p_n, \mathcal{M}) \leq \frac{C_1\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}{n^{r_0}}= \mathcal{O}(n^{-r_0}),
	\end{equation}
	\begin{equation} \norm{\hat p_n - \mathbf{p}} \leq C_2\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) \left(\frac{ n}{\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)^2}\right)^{-r_1} = \wtilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{-r_1})  ,
	\end{equation}
	and 
	\begin{equation} \angle_{\max}(\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}},T_{\mathbf p}\mathcal{M}) \leq C_3\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) \left(\frac{ n}{\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)^2}\right)^{-r_1} = \wtilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{-r_1})    
	\end{equation}
	with probability of at least $ 1 - \delta $, where $ r_0 = \frac{k}{2k +d}, r_1 = \frac{k-1}{2k +d} $, and $ C_1,C_2,C_3$ are constants independent of $d, \delta$.
assumptions: Assume that $M>C_\tau\sqrt{D\log D}$.
Let $(q, H)$ be an initial coordinate system for which $\norm{q - p}\leq 3 \sigma$ and $ \angle_{\max} (H, T_p\mathcal{M}) \leq \sqrt{c_{M}/M}$, where $p= Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(q) \in \mathcal{M}$.
conclusions: with probability of at least $ 1 - \delta $, where $ r_0 = \frac{k}{2k +d}, r_1 = \frac{k-1}{2k +d} $, and $ C_1,C_2,C_3$ are constants independent of $d, \delta$.
nodes.statement_short: From a coarse initialization, Algorithm 2 with $\kappa$ iterations gives $\hat p_n$ and tangent with errors $O(n^{-r_0})$ to $\mathcal{M}$ and $\tilde O(n^{-r_1})$ to the projection.
nodes.label: thm:Step2

nodes.name: Distance of hat p_n to M
nodes.statement: dist(\hat p_n, \mathcal{M}) \leq \frac{C_1\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}{n^{r_0}}= \mathcal{O}(n^{-r_0}),
nodes.label: eq:thm3.3_p_dist_bound

nodes.name: Distance of hat p_n to the projection
nodes.statement: \norm{\hat p_n - \mathbf{p}} \leq C_2\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) \left(\frac{ n}{\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)^2}\right)^{-r_1} = \wtilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{-r_1})  ,
nodes.label: eq:thm3.3_p_bound

nodes.name: Tangent angle bound
nodes.statement: \angle_{\max}(\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}},T_{\mathbf p}\mathcal{M}) \leq C_3\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) \left(\frac{ n}{\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)^2}\right)^{-r_1} = \wtilde{\mathcal{O}}(n^{-r_1})
nodes.label: eq:thm3.3_tangent_ang

nodes.name: Expected distance to the manifold
nodes.statement:
Note that since the errors in the manifold and tangent estimation are bounded we can also conclude from Theorem \ref{thm:MainResult}, by choosing $\delta = n^{-r_0}$, that
\[
E(dist(\hat p_n, \mathcal{M})) \leq C_4 n^{-r_0}.
\]
assumptions: the errors in the manifold and tangent estimation are bounded

nodes.name: Expected tangent angle error
nodes.statement:
Similarly, by choosing $\delta = n^{-r_1}$, we have
\[
E(\angle_{\max}(\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}},T_{\hat p}\mathcal{M})) \leq  C_5\left(\frac{ n}{\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)^2}\right)^{-r_1}.
\]

nodes.name: Rates are sub-optimal compared to Genovese et al.
nodes.statement:
We wish to note here that although we show convergence to the underlying manifold when $n\to\infty$ the convergence rates we achieve are sub-optimal in the case of $k=2$ as observed by Genovese et. al. \cite{genovese2012minimax} where the optimal rates for manifold estimation in the Hausdorff sense are shown to be $\mathcal{O}(n^{-2/(2+d)})$. 
This analysis combined with the fact shown by Amaari and Levrard \cite{aamari2019nonasymptotic} lends the possibility that the optimal rates for manifold estimation should be $\mathcal{O}(n^{-k/(k+d)})$, which are not achieved here.
However, the convergence rates we achieve here rely on the rates for local polynomial estimation, which are known to be optimal for non-parametric point estimation of functions.
nodes.statement_short: The achieved rates are sub-optimal for $k=2$ relative to known minimax manifold-estimation rates, but rest on optimal local polynomial regression rates.

nodes.name: Rates of the algorithm are tight
nodes.statement: Thus, we believe that our analysis of the algorithm represents its true rates of convergence rather than just bounding them.

nodes.name: Rates persist for whole-manifold estimation
nodes.statement: While the presented approach may be extended to estimating the entire manifold, and the current bounds may be extended to bound the Hausdorff distance between the estimated manifold and the underling manifold, we believe that the convergence rates will stay as they are.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement:
The proof can be described by the following three arguments which are proven in Lemmas \ref{lem:J1pTp_clean}, \ref{lem:J_1qH_clean}.
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[Arg. 1:] Denote $p_r = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$.
		Then, since $r - p_r\perp T_{p_r}\mathcal{M} $ and $r\in\mathcal{M}_\sigma$, we have that $q = p_r$ along with $H= T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}$ are in the search space defined by the constraints of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean}.
		
		\item[Arg. 2:] From Lemma \ref{lem:J1pTp_clean} it follows that for large enough $M = \tau/\sigma$ such that $ \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}  + \frac{\sigma}{\tau} < \frac{1}{2} $ we have $J_1(r; p_r; T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}) \leq 50\cdot \sigma^2$. 
		According to Assumption \ref{assume:noise} in Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions}, we have that $M$ is large enough, and Lemma \ref{lem:J1pTp_clean} hold.
		Due to the definition of $q^*, H^*$ in \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean}, we achieve that $J_1(r; q^*, H^*) \leq 50 \cdot \sigma^2$ as well.
		
		\item[Arg. 3:] From Lemma \ref{lem:J_1qH_clean}, we have that  
		for $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$, where $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, and $C_{M}$ is a constant
		the following holds:
		For any $\delta >0$ arbitrarily small there is $ N_{\delta} $ sufficiently large (independent of $\alpha$) such that for all $ n>N_{\delta} $, \textbf{all} pairs $(q, H)$ in the search space of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean} such that $\angle_{max}(H,T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}) > \alpha$, the score $J_1(r; q, H) \geq 100 \sigma^2 $ with probability of at least $1 - \delta$.
	\end{enumerate}
	Combining Arguments 2 and 3 we have that 
	for $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$, where $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, and $C_{M}$ is a constant
	the following holds:
	For any $\delta>0$ arbitrarily small, there exists $ N_{\delta} $ (independent of $\alpha$) such that for all $ n > N_{\delta} $ 
	\[\angle_{\max}(H^*, T_p\mathcal{M})\leq \alpha\]
	with probability of at least $ 1 - \delta $. Additionally, since the search space of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean} requires that $\|r-q^*\| <2\sigma$, we have that $\|p-q^*\|\leq 3\sigma$, and the proof is concluded.
nodes.statement_short: The true projection and tangent are feasible with score $\le 50\sigma^2$, while any subspace tilted by more than $\alpha$ scores $\ge 100\sigma^2$ w.h.p.; so the minimizer is $\alpha$-close.

nodes.name: Outline of three arguments
nodes.statement:
The proof can be described by the following three arguments which are proven in Lemmas \ref{lem:J1pTp_clean}, \ref{lem:J_1qH_clean}.
	\begin{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Announce three arguments proven via Lemmas 4.1 and 4.3.

nodes.name: Arg. 1: true projection is feasible
nodes.statement:
[Arg. 1:] Denote $p_r = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$.
		Then, since $r - p_r\perp T_{p_r}\mathcal{M} $ and $r\in\mathcal{M}_\sigma$, we have that $q = p_r$ along with $H= T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}$ are in the search space defined by the constraints of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean}.
nodes.statement_short: The projection $p_r$ with its tangent lies in the search space.

nodes.name: Arg. 2: small score at the tangent
nodes.statement:
[Arg. 2:] From Lemma \ref{lem:J1pTp_clean} it follows that for large enough $M = \tau/\sigma$ such that $ \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}}  + \frac{\sigma}{\tau} < \frac{1}{2} $ we have $J_1(r; p_r; T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}) \leq 50\cdot \sigma^2$. 
		According to Assumption \ref{assume:noise} in Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions}, we have that $M$ is large enough, and Lemma \ref{lem:J1pTp_clean} hold.
		Due to the definition of $q^*, H^*$ in \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean}, we achieve that $J_1(r; q^*, H^*) \leq 50 \cdot \sigma^2$ as well.
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 4.1 the tangent scores at most $50\sigma^2$, hence so does the minimizer.

nodes.name: Arg. 3: tilted subspaces score high
nodes.statement:
[Arg. 3:] From Lemma \ref{lem:J_1qH_clean}, we have that  
		for $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$, where $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, and $C_{M}$ is a constant
		the following holds:
		For any $\delta >0$ arbitrarily small there is $ N_{\delta} $ sufficiently large (independent of $\alpha$) such that for all $ n>N_{\delta} $, \textbf{all} pairs $(q, H)$ in the search space of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean} such that $\angle_{max}(H,T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}) > \alpha$, the score $J_1(r; q, H) \geq 100 \sigma^2 $ with probability of at least $1 - \delta$.
	\end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: By Lemma 4.3 tilted subspaces score at least $100\sigma^2$ w.h.p.

nodes.name: Combine arguments
nodes.statement:
Combining Arguments 2 and 3 we have that 
	for $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$, where $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, and $C_{M}$ is a constant
	the following holds:
	For any $\delta>0$ arbitrarily small, there exists $ N_{\delta} $ (independent of $\alpha$) such that for all $ n > N_{\delta} $ 
	\[\angle_{\max}(H^*, T_p\mathcal{M})\leq \alpha\]
	with probability of at least $ 1 - \delta $. Additionally, since the search space of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean} requires that $\|r-q^*\| <2\sigma$, we have that $\|p-q^*\|\leq 3\sigma$, and the proof is concluded.
nodes.statement_short: Arguments 2 and 3 force $H^*$ to be within angle $\alpha$; the search constraint gives $\|p-q^*\|\le3\sigma$.

nodes.name: Tangent score bound J_1 <= 50 sigma^2
nodes.statement:
Let the sampling assumption of \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions} hold, let ${p_r} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$ be the orthogonal projection of $r$ onto $\mathcal{M}$, and let $ T_{p_r}\mathcal{M} $ be the tangent to $ \mathcal{M} $ at $ {p_r} $.
	Then, for $M$ (of Assumption \ref{assume:noise}) large enough
	\begin{equation} J_1(r; {p_r}, T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) \leq 50 \cdot \sigma^2 
	\end{equation}
assumptions: Let the sampling assumption of \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions} hold
let ${p_r} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$ be the orthogonal projection of $r$ onto $\mathcal{M}$
for $M$ (of Assumption \ref{assume:noise}) large enough
nodes.label: lem:J1pTp_clean

nodes.name: Tangent score bound
nodes.statement: J_1(r; {p_r}, T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) \leq 50 \cdot \sigma^2
nodes.label: eq:TangentScore_clean

nodes.name: Idea of the proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement: \textbf{Idea of the proof: } Since all the sampled points are $\sigma$-close to the manifold which is linearly approximated by the tangent, the mean squared distance to the tangent is of the order of $\mathcal{O}(\sigma^2)$.
nodes.statement_short: Samples are $\sigma$-close to a manifold that the tangent approximates linearly, so the mean squared distance is $O(\sigma^2)$.

nodes.name: Tilted subspaces through p_r score at least 109 sigma^2
nodes.statement:
Let the sampling assumptions of Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions} hold.
	Let ${p_r} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$ be the projection of $r$ onto $\mathcal{M}$, and $ T_{p_r}\mathcal{M} $ be the tangent to $ \mathcal{M} $ at $ {p_r} $. 
	For $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$, where $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, and $C_{M}$ is a constant,
	the following holds: For any $\delta >0$ there is $N_\delta$ (independent of $\alpha$) such that $\forall n > N_\delta$ all linear sub-spaces $H\in Gr(d,D)$ with $\angle_{max}(H,T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) > \alpha$, yield a score 
	\[J_1(r; {p_r}, H) \geq 109 \sigma^2 ,\]
	with probability of at least $1 - \delta$.
assumptions: Let the sampling assumptions of Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions} hold.
For $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$, where $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, and $C_{M}$ is a constant,
nodes.statement_short: W.h.p., every subspace through $p_r$ tilted by more than $\alpha$ from the tangent has score $J_1\ge109\sigma^2$.
nodes.label: thm:J1pH_clean

nodes.name: Tilted coordinate systems score at least 100 sigma^2
nodes.statement:
Let the sampling assumption of Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions} hold. Let ${p_r} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$ be the projection of $r$ onto $\mathcal{M}$, and $ T_{p_r}\mathcal{M} $ be the tangent to $ \mathcal{M} $ at $ {p_r} $.
	For $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$, where $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, and $C_{M}$ is a constant  the following holds:
	For any $\delta >0$ there is $N_\delta$ (independent of $\alpha$) such that $\forall n > N_\delta$ all linear sub-spaces $H \in Gr(d,D)$ with $\angle_{max}(H,T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) > \alpha$, and all $q$ in the search space of \eqref{eq:argmin1_clean} yield a score 
	\[
	J_1(r; {q}, H) \geq 100\sigma^2 
	\]
	with probability of at least $1 - \delta$.
assumptions: Let the sampling assumption of Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions} hold.
For $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$, where $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, and $C_{M}$ is a constant
nodes.statement_short: W.h.p., every feasible $(q,H)$ with $H$ tilted by more than $\alpha$ has score $J_1\ge100\sigma^2$.
nodes.label: lem:J_1qH_clean

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement:
From Lemma \ref{thm:J1pH_clean}, we have that there is a constant $C_{M}$ such that for any $ {\alpha} < \frac{\pi}{2} $ and $M = C_{M}/\alpha^2$, and for any $\tau$ and $\sigma$ maintaining $\frac{\tau}{\sigma}>M$
	the following hold:
	For any $\delta >0$ arbitrarily small there is $ N_\delta $ sufficiently large such that for all $ n>N_\delta $, \textbf{all} linear spaces $H$ with $\angle_{max}(H,T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}) > \alpha$, yield a score $J_1(r; p_r, H) \geq 109 \cdot \sigma^2 $, with probability of at least $1 - \delta$. 
	We now wish to show that $J_1(r; q, H) \geq 100 \sigma^2$ with high probability as well.
	For convenience we wish to reiterate \eqref{eq:J1_clean}
	\[
	J_1(r; q, H) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{r_i\in U_{\textrm{ROI}}} \operatorname{dist}^2 (r_i - q,H)
	.\]
	By Constraint 3 of \eqref{eq:J1_clean} we achieve that $dist(q, \mathcal{M}) \leq 3\sigma$ and so for $p=Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(q)$ we have
	$
	\norm{q - p} \leq 3\sigma
	$.
	Thus,
	\[
	\operatorname{dist}^2 (r_i - q,H) = \norm{p - q}^2 + \operatorname{dist}^2 (r_i - p,H) \geq \operatorname{dist}^2 (r_i - p,H) - 9\sigma^2
	,\]
	and we achieve
	$
	J_1(r; q, H) \geq J_1(r; p, H) - 9\sigma^2
	$.
	By Lemma \ref{thm:J1pH_clean} we conclude the proof of the current lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Shift the origin from $p_r$ to $q$ at a cost of at most $9\sigma^2$ in $J_1$ and apply Lemma 4.2.

nodes.name: Recall Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement:
From Lemma \ref{thm:J1pH_clean}, we have that there is a constant $C_{M}$ such that for any $ {\alpha} < \frac{\pi}{2} $ and $M = C_{M}/\alpha^2$, and for any $\tau$ and $\sigma$ maintaining $\frac{\tau}{\sigma}>M$
	the following hold:
	For any $\delta >0$ arbitrarily small there is $ N_\delta $ sufficiently large such that for all $ n>N_\delta $, \textbf{all} linear spaces $H$ with $\angle_{max}(H,T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}) > \alpha$, yield a score $J_1(r; p_r, H) \geq 109 \cdot \sigma^2 $, with probability of at least $1 - \delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.2 gives score $\ge109\sigma^2$ at origin $p_r$.

nodes.name: Goal and recall of J_1
nodes.statement:
We now wish to show that $J_1(r; q, H) \geq 100 \sigma^2$ with high probability as well.
	For convenience we wish to reiterate \eqref{eq:J1_clean}
	\[
	J_1(r; q, H) = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{r_i\in U_{\textrm{ROI}}} \operatorname{dist}^2 (r_i - q,H)
	.\]
nodes.statement_short: State the goal and recall the definition of $J_1$.

nodes.name: Origin shift costs 9 sigma^2
nodes.statement:
By Constraint 3 of \eqref{eq:J1_clean} we achieve that $dist(q, \mathcal{M}) \leq 3\sigma$ and so for $p=Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(q)$ we have
	$
	\norm{q - p} \leq 3\sigma
	$.
	Thus,
	\[
	\operatorname{dist}^2 (r_i - q,H) = \norm{p - q}^2 + \operatorname{dist}^2 (r_i - p,H) \geq \operatorname{dist}^2 (r_i - p,H) - 9\sigma^2
	,\]
	and we achieve
	$
	J_1(r; q, H) \geq J_1(r; p, H) - 9\sigma^2
	$.
nodes.statement_short: Since $\|q-p\|\le3\sigma$, $J_1(r;q,H)\ge J_1(r;p,H)-9\sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: By Lemma \ref{thm:J1pH_clean} we conclude the proof of the current lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 4.2.

nodes.name: Initial direction H_0
nodes.statement: As Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean} involves an iterative process, we denote the initial directions of the tangent estimation as $H_0 := H$.

nodes.name: Initial local function f_0 and cylinder Cyl
nodes.statement_short: View the manifold patch inside a cylinder over $H_0$ as the graph of $f_0$ over $(r,H_0)$.

nodes.name: Graph of f_0
nodes.statement:
\Gamma_{f_{0}, r,H_0} \stackrel{\bigtriangleup}{=} \{r + (x, f_{0}(x))_{H_0} ~|~ x\in B_{H_0}(0, c_{\pi/4}\tau)\}  
	,

nodes.name: alpha small enough
nodes.statement: For the remainder of this section, we assume that $ \alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M} $ is small enough (see the sampling assumptions in Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions}).

nodes.name: Fibre Omega_l(x) of the tubular neighborhood
nodes.statement:
However, in our case, for any $x\in H_\ell$, the samples above $x$ are uniformly distributed~in 
\begin{equation} \Omega_\ell(x) = (x + H_\ell^\perp) \cap  \mathcal{M}_\sigma
	,\end{equation}
where $x + H_\ell^\perp = \{x + y ~|~ y\in H_\ell^\perp\}$.
That is, $\Omega_\ell(x):H_\ell \simeq \mathbb{R}^d \to 2^{\mathbb{R}^{D-d}}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Omega_\ell(x)$ is the slice of $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ above $x$ in the normal directions of $H_\ell$; samples above $x$ are uniform on it.

nodes.name: Omega_l(x)
nodes.statement:
\Omega_\ell(x) = (x + H_\ell^\perp) \cap  \mathcal{M}_\sigma
	,
nodes.label: eq:Omega_def

nodes.name: Regression function tilde f_l
nodes.statement:
Thus, denoting $\eta_\ell(x)\sim \textrm{Unif}(\Omega(x))$ and defining 
\begin{equation} \wtilde f_\ell(x) = \mathbb{E}[\eta_\ell(y | x)]     \neq f_\ell
	,\end{equation}
the result of the regression will estimate $\wtilde f_\ell$ rather than $f_\ell$ itself  (see Figure \ref{fig:TiltedBias}).
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde f_\ell$ is the conditional mean of the uniform noise over $\Omega_\ell(x)$; regression estimates it rather than $f_\ell$.

nodes.name: tilde f_l as conditional expectation
nodes.statement:
\wtilde f_\ell(x) = \mathbb{E}[\eta_\ell(y | x)]     \neq f_\ell
	,
nodes.label: eq:ftilde_def

nodes.name: Angle-halving lemma for one iteration of Step 2
nodes.statement:
Let $H_\ell\in Gr(d, D)$, and let $f_\ell:H_\ell\simeq\mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$, defined as in \eqref{eq:fl_def}. Define $H_{\ell+1} = \mathrm{Im}(\mathcal{D}_{\pi^*_{q_\ell,H_{\ell}}}[0])$, as in Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean}, and let $r_1 = \frac{k-1}{2k +d}$. 
	Assume that $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma} \geq C_\tau \sqrt{D\log D}$ (where $C_\tau$ is a constant from Lemma \ref{lem:Tf_TtildeF_D}).
	For any $\delta>0$, there is $N$ such that for any number of samples $n>N$, and any $\alpha \leq\sqrt{1/D}$ smaller than some constant \emph{(}see Theorem \ref{thm:Step1} and Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions} for the definition of $M$ and $C_{M}$\emph{)}.  If
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item $\angle_{\max} (H_\ell, T_0 f_\ell) = \alpha_\ell\leq \alpha$
		\item $\|f_\ell(0)\| \leq \min (c_{\pi/4} \cdot \tau, \sqrt{\tau/32} -1) $
		\item $N$ satisfies $ 12\sqrt{d} \frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{N^{r_1}}\leq \alpha $ 
	\end{enumerate}
	hold, where $C_0$ is some constant. Then, we have  
	\[
	\alpha_{\ell+1} = \angle_{\max} (H_{\ell+1}, T_0 f_{\ell+1})  = \angle_{\max} (H_{\ell+1}, T_0 f_{\ell+1/2}) \leq \alpha/2
	\]
	and
	\[
	\|f_{\ell+1}(0)\| \leq \|f_\ell(0)\|\left(1+40\alpha^2\right) 
	\]
	with probability at least $1-\delta$.
assumptions: Let $H_\ell\in Gr(d, D)$, and let $f_\ell:H_\ell\simeq\mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$, defined as in \eqref{eq:fl_def}.
Assume that $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma} \geq C_\tau \sqrt{D\log D}$
$\angle_{\max} (H_\ell, T_0 f_\ell) = \alpha_\ell\leq \alpha$
$\|f_\ell(0)\| \leq \min (c_{\pi/4} \cdot \tau, \sqrt{\tau/32} -1) $
$N$ satisfies $ 12\sqrt{d} \frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta)}{N^{r_1}}\leq \alpha $
nodes.statement_short: One iteration of Algorithm 2 halves the angle between the coordinate system and the tangent while growing $\|f_\ell(0)\|$ by at most a $(1+40\alpha^2)$ factor, w.h.p.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement:
We divide Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean} into four steps:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item[(i)] Show that the initialization $H_0 $ results with $\angle_{\max}(H_0, T_{0} f_0)$ and $\|f_0(0)\|$ small enough (using Lemmas \ref{lem:H0_Tf_Init} and \ref{lem:dist_to_f_00}).
		\item[(ii)] Show that estimating $H_{\ell+1}$ from $H_{\ell}$ (with the origin set at $r$) improves the angle  $\angle_{\max}(H_\ell, T_{0} f_\ell)$ - corresponds to rows 4 to 6 in Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean} (using Lemma \ref{lem:main_support_theorem_step2}).
		\item[(iii)] We show that for $\mathrm{\mathbf{p}} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$ - the projection of $r$ onto $\mathcal{M}$, $\angle_{\max}(H_\kappa, T_{\mathrm{\mathbf{p}}}\mathcal{M})$  is small (as required in \eqref{eq:thm3.3_tangent_ang}) (Using Lemmas \ref{lem:dist_given_angle}).
		\item[(iv)] Show that $\hat p_n$  is a good estimate of  $\mathrm{\mathbf{p}}$ - corresponds to row 8 in Algorithm \ref{alg:step2_clean} (using Lemma~\ref{lem:dist_to_f_l0_srtong_small_alpha}).
	\end{enumerate}
	Note that step (ii) is repeated $\kappa$ times.
	Below, we treat the four steps one by one. 
	Although we prove this point later, we start by assuming that $\kappa$ and $\delta_1$ are
	\begin{equation} 12\sqrt{d}\frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta_1)}{n^{r_1}} \leq \alpha_0 2^{-\kappa+1},
	\end{equation}
	where $C_0$ is the constant from Lemma \ref{lem:main_support_theorem_step2}. 
	
	\paragraph*{Step (i):}
	Let $\alpha_0=\sqrt{1/D}$ and denote by $A_0$ the event of
	\[
	\angle_{\max} (T_0f_{0}, H_{0}) \leq \alpha_0 
	~~~~\mbox{ and } ~~~~
	\|f_0(0)\| \leq 10\sigma 
	.\]
	From Lemma \ref{lem:H0_Tf_Init} and Theorem \ref{thm:Step1} that for $M$ large enough, there is $N_{1,\delta_1}$ such that for all $n>N_{1,\delta_1}$ we have that:
	\[
	\Pr\left(\angle_{\max} (T_0f_{0}, H_{0}) \leq \alpha_0 \right) \geq 1-\delta_1,
	.\]
	From Lemma \ref{lem:dist_to_f_00} we have that
	\[
	\Pr\left(\|f_0(0)\| \leq 10\sigma \right) \geq 1-\delta_1.
	\]
	This means that $P(A_0) \geq 1-\delta_1$ (note that the failure probability comes from Theorem \ref{thm:Step1}, and once the result of the theorem holds, the conditions of Lemmas \ref{lem:H0_Tf_Init}, \ref{lem:dist_to_f_00} are met).

	
	\paragraph*{Step(ii):}
	Denote by $A_\ell$ the event that $\angle_{\max} (T_0f_{\ell}, H_{\ell}) \leq \alpha_0 2^{-\ell} = \alpha_{\ell}$ and also
	\[
	\|f_\ell(0)\| \leq \|f_{\ell-1}(0)\|\left(1+40\alpha_{\ell-1}^2\right)
	.\]
	We now wish to apply Lemma \ref{lem:main_support_theorem_step2} in an iterated fashion.
	To initiate the iterative process, we have to assume that $n$ is at least $N_{2, \delta_1} = \left( \frac{12\sqrt{d}C_0\ln(1/\delta)}{\alpha_0}\right)^{1/r_1}$ (i.e., requirement 3 of the Lemma).
	To comply with requirement 3 of Lemma \ref{lem:main_support_theorem_step2} in all the following iterations, the total number of iterations $ \kappa$ that we can perform is limited by the actual number of samples~$n$ (since  $\alpha$ shrinks with each iteration).
	Below, we show what should be the value of $\kappa$ that allows for the iterated application of Lemma \ref{lem:main_support_theorem_step2} given $n$.
	
	Since $M>C_\tau \sqrt{D\log D}$, and $\alpha_0 \leq \sqrt{ 1/D}$ if events $A_0, \ldots, A_\ell$ hold, then the requirements of Lemma \ref{lem:main_support_theorem_step2} are met for $\alpha = \alpha_\ell = \alpha_0 2^{-\ell}$. 
	The only nontrivial requirement is the bound on $\|f_\ell(0)\|$. Since all the events $A_{i}$ for $i\leq \ell$ hold we have
	\begin{align*}
		\|f_\ell(0)\| &\leq \|f_{\ell-1}(0)\|\left(1+40\alpha_{\ell-1}^2  \right) \nonumber
		\\
		&\leq \|f_{\ell-2}(0)\|\left(1+40\alpha_{\ell-2}^2 \right)\left(1+40\alpha_{\ell-1}^2  \right) \nonumber
		\\
		&\leq \|f_{0}(0)\|\prod_{i=0}^{\ell} \left(1+40\alpha_{i}^2  \right)
		\\
		&\leq \|f_{0}(0)\|\prod_{i=0}^{\ell} \left(1+40\alpha_0^2 2^{-2i} \right)
	\end{align*}
	Denote $a_0 = 40\alpha_0 ^2$, and then
	\begin{align*}
		\|f_\ell(0)\| &\leq \|f_{0}(0)\|\prod_{i=0}^{\ell} \left(1+a_0 2^{-2i} \right)
		\\
		& = \|f_{0}(0)\|\exp\left(\sum_{i=0}^{\ell} \ln\left(1+a_0 2^{-2i} \right)\right)
		\\
		& \leq \|f_{0}(0)\|\exp\left(\sum_{i=0}^{\ell} a_0 2^{-2i} \right)
		\\
		& \leq \|f_{0}(0)\|\exp\left(\sum_{i=0}^{\infty} a_0 2^{-2i} \right)
		\\
		& \leq \|f_{0}(0)\|\exp\left(2a_0  \right)
	\end{align*}
	
	Thus, we have that for $n> N_{2,\delta_1}$, with probability of at least $1-\delta_1$, the event $A_{\ell+1}$ holds given events $A_0, \ldots, A_{\ell}$ hold for any $\ell \leq \kappa$.
	
	

	
	To conclude our arguments so far, since $\kappa$ satisfies \eqref{eq:n_bound1}, using the union bound on the events $A_0,\ldots, A_\kappa$  we have that 
	\begin{equation} \Pr\left(\angle_{\max} (T_0 f_{\kappa}, H_{\kappa}) \leq \alpha_0 2^{-\kappa}\right) \geq 1 -  \kappa\delta_1.        
	\end{equation}
	Choosing $\delta_1 = \frac{\delta}{\kappa+1}$, we have from Lemma \ref{lem:comute_kappa}, that $\kappa$ from \eqref{eq:kappa_res_lem} satisfies  \eqref{eq:n_bound1}. We also have from Lemma \ref{lem:comute_kappa} that 
	\[
	\alpha_0 2^{-\kappa} \leq \tilde C_{d} \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}.
	\]
	Thus, we have that 
	\begin{equation} \angle_{\max} (Tf_{\kappa}(0), H_{\kappa}) \leq \tilde C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1},    
	\end{equation}
	given events $A_0,\ldots A_\kappa$ hold.
	\paragraph*{Step (iii):} Denote by $p_{\kappa}=(r,f_\kappa(0))_{r, H_{\kappa}}$, and $\mathrm{\mathbf{p}} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$. Applying Lemma \ref{lem:dist_given_angle} we have that 
	\begin{equation} \|\mathrm{\mathbf{p}} - p_{\kappa}\| \leq \frac{\hat C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\left(\frac{1}{2\sigma(2+\sigma/\tau)}-\frac{c}{\tau} \right)},
	\end{equation}
	with probability of at least $1-\delta$. From Corollary 3 in \cite{boissonnat2017reach}, we have that 
	\begin{equation} \sin \frac{\angle_{\max}(T_{\mathbf{p}}\mathcal{M},Tf_\kappa(0))}{2} \leq \frac{\|\mathrm{\mathbf{p}}-p_\kappa\|}{2\tau}.
	\end{equation}
	or,
	\begin{equation} \angle_{\max}(T_{\mathbf{p}}\mathcal{M},Tf_\kappa(0)) \leq \frac{2\|\mathrm{\mathbf{p}}-p_\kappa\|}{\tau}.
	\end{equation}
	Combining \ref{eq:TPM_Tfk} and \eqref{eq:P_q_dist_bound} we have 
	\begin{equation} \angle_{\max}(T_{\mathbf{p}}\mathcal{M},Tf_\kappa(0))
		\leq \frac{2\hat C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\tau\left(\frac{1}{2\sigma(2+\sigma/\tau)}-\frac{c}{\tau} \right)} = 
		\frac{2\hat C_{d}\ln\left(
			\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\frac{M}{4 + 2/M} -c} 
		,
	\end{equation}
	given events $A_0,\ldots A_\kappa$ hold.
	Note that the expression $\frac{M}{4 + 2/M} -c $ in \eqref{eq:TPM_Tfk_full} grows with $M$.
	Combining \eqref{eq:TPM_Tfk_full} with \eqref{eq:prob_ang_bound_Tfk_Hk}, and using the triangle inequality, we get 
	\begin{equation} \angle_{\max}(T_{\mathbf{p}}\mathcal{M},H_\kappa) \leq C_d \cdot \ln(1/\delta)n^{-r_1} (\ln \ln(n))^{2 r_1}
	\end{equation}
	given events $A_0,\ldots A_\kappa$ hold, where $C_d$ is some general constant. 
	Note that according to Algorithm~\ref{alg:step2_clean}  $\widehat{T_{\hat p_n}\mathcal{M}} = H_\kappa$.
	
	\paragraph*{Step (iv):} In order to bound the error $\|\hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\|$ we use the triangle inequality 
	\[
	\|\hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\| \leq \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa\| + \| p_\kappa - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\|, 
	\]
	where $p_\kappa = (r,f_\kappa(0))_{H_{\kappa}}$,
	and bound the two parts in the right hand side separately.
	
	The first part, $\| p_\kappa - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\| $ is bounded in \eqref{eq:P_q_dist_bound}.
	
	Furthermore, assuming event $A_\kappa$ holds, since $\alpha = \alpha_0 2^{-\kappa}<1/D$, there is $N_3$ such that for $n>N_{3}$ we have from Lemma \ref{lem:dist_to_f_l0_srtong_small_alpha} that  
	\[
	\|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq 8 \sigma D \alpha_1^2 2^{-2\kappa} + \frac{c\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}{n^{r_0}}
	\]
	holds with probability at least $1-\delta/(\kappa+1)$, where $c$ is some general constant and $ r_0 = \frac{k}{2k +d}$. Explicitly. 
	Denote this event by~$B$.
	Substituting $\kappa$ from \eqref{eq:kappa_res_lem} we have from Lemma \ref{lem:comute_kappa} that 
	\[
	\| \hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq 8\sigma D C_{d}^2 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)^2 n^{-2r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{4r_1} + c\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)n^{-r_0}
	\]
	or, for $n$ large enough, and some constant $ C_1$,
	\begin{equation} \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq C_1 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_0}.
	\end{equation}
	Note that $p_\kappa \in \mathcal{M}$, so $dist(\hat p_n,\mathcal{M}) \leq \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \|$.
	
	Combining this with \eqref{eq:P_q_dist_bound}, assuming events $A_0,\ldots A_\kappa,B$ hold, we have that 
	\[
	\| \hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\|  \leq  C_1 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_0} + \frac{\hat C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\left(\frac{1}{2\sigma(2+\sigma/\tau)}-\frac{c}{\tau} \right)}.
	\] 
	Alternatively, for $n$ large enough, and some constant $C$, given the events $A_1,\ldots, A_\kappa, B$ hold, 
	\begin{equation} \|\hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\| \leq C\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}  \left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}.    
	\end{equation}
	Using the union bound on $A_1,\ldots, A_\kappa, B$, we have that Equations \eqref{eq:res_thm33_tang}, \eqref{eq:pnhat-pkappa_bound} and \eqref{eq:pn-p_bound} are satisfied with probability of at least $1 - \delta$.
	This concludes the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:Step2}.

	\]
	Thus, we have that 
	\begin{equation} \angle_{\max} (Tf_{\kappa}(0), H_{\kappa}) \leq \tilde C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1},    
	\end{equation}
	given events $A_0,\ldots A_\kappa$ hold.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 10.4 gives the final angle bound $\tilde O(n^{-r_1})$.

nodes.name: Step (iii): tangent at the projection
nodes.statement_short: Convert the angle bound into a distance bound (Lemma 10.26) and back into an angle at $\mathbf{p}$.

nodes.name: Distance of p_kappa to p
nodes.statement:
Denote by $p_{\kappa}=(r,f_\kappa(0))_{r, H_{\kappa}}$, and $\mathrm{\mathbf{p}} = Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r)$. Applying Lemma \ref{lem:dist_given_angle} we have that 
	\begin{equation} \|\mathrm{\mathbf{p}} - p_{\kappa}\| \leq \frac{\hat C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\left(\frac{1}{2\sigma(2+\sigma/\tau)}-\frac{c}{\tau} \right)},
	\end{equation}
	with probability of at least $1-\delta$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 10.26 bounds $\|\mathbf{p}-p_\kappa\|$.

nodes.name: Reach bounds tangent variation
nodes.statement_short: Tangent angles vary at most like distance over $\tau$.

nodes.name: Angle between T_pM and T f_kappa
nodes.statement:
Combining \ref{eq:TPM_Tfk} and \eqref{eq:P_q_dist_bound} we have 
	\begin{equation} \angle_{\max}(T_{\mathbf{p}}\mathcal{M},Tf_\kappa(0))
		\leq \frac{2\hat C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\tau\left(\frac{1}{2\sigma(2+\sigma/\tau)}-\frac{c}{\tau} \right)} = 
		\frac{2\hat C_{d}\ln\left(
			\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\frac{M}{4 + 2/M} -c} 
		,
	\end{equation}
	given events $A_0,\ldots A_\kappa$ hold.
	Note that the expression $\frac{M}{4 + 2/M} -c $ in \eqref{eq:TPM_Tfk_full} grows with $M$.
nodes.statement_short: Combine to bound the angle between $T_{\mathbf{p}}\mathcal{M}$ and $Tf_\kappa(0)$.

nodes.name: Tangent error bound
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality gives the tangent error of $H_\kappa$.

nodes.name: Step (iv): point estimate
nodes.statement:
\paragraph*{Step (iv):} In order to bound the error $\|\hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\|$ we use the triangle inequality 
	\[
	\|\hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\| \leq \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa\| + \| p_\kappa - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\|, 
	\]
	where $p_\kappa = (r,f_\kappa(0))_{H_{\kappa}}$,
	and bound the two parts in the right hand side separately.
	
	The first part, $\| p_\kappa - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\| $ is bounded in \eqref{eq:P_q_dist_bound}.
	
	Furthermore, assuming event $A_\kappa$ holds, since $\alpha = \alpha_0 2^{-\kappa}<1/D$, there is $N_3$ such that for $n>N_{3}$ we have from Lemma \ref{lem:dist_to_f_l0_srtong_small_alpha} that  
	\[
	\|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq 8 \sigma D \alpha_1^2 2^{-2\kappa} + \frac{c\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}{n^{r_0}}
	\]
	holds with probability at least $1-\delta/(\kappa+1)$, where $c$ is some general constant and $ r_0 = \frac{k}{2k +d}$. Explicitly. 
	Denote this event by~$B$.
	Substituting $\kappa$ from \eqref{eq:kappa_res_lem} we have from Lemma \ref{lem:comute_kappa} that 
	\[
	\| \hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq 8\sigma D C_{d}^2 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)^2 n^{-2r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{4r_1} + c\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)n^{-r_0}
	\]
	or, for $n$ large enough, and some constant $ C_1$,
	\begin{equation} \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq C_1 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_0}.
	\end{equation}
	Note that $p_\kappa \in \mathcal{M}$, so $dist(\hat p_n,\mathcal{M}) \leq \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \|$.
	
	Combining this with \eqref{eq:P_q_dist_bound}, assuming events $A_0,\ldots A_\kappa,B$ hold, we have that 
	\[
	\| \hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\|  \leq  C_1 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_0} + \frac{\hat C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\left(\frac{1}{2\sigma(2+\sigma/\tau)}-\frac{c}{\tau} \right)}.
	\] 
	Alternatively, for $n$ large enough, and some constant $C$, given the events $A_1,\ldots, A_\kappa, B$ hold, 
	\begin{equation} \|\hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\| \leq C\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}  \left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}.    
	\end{equation}
	Using the union bound on $A_1,\ldots, A_\kappa, B$, we have that Equations \eqref{eq:res_thm33_tang}, \eqref{eq:pnhat-pkappa_bound} and \eqref{eq:pn-p_bound} are satisfied with probability of at least $1 - \delta$.
	This concludes the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:Step2}.
nodes.statement_short: Triangle inequality with Lemma 10.23 and Step (iii), then a final union bound.

nodes.name: Split by triangle inequality
nodes.statement:
In order to bound the error $\|\hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\|$ we use the triangle inequality 
	\[
	\|\hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\| \leq \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa\| + \| p_\kappa - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\|, 
	\]
	where $p_\kappa = (r,f_\kappa(0))_{H_{\kappa}}$,
	and bound the two parts in the right hand side separately.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\|\hat p_n-\mathbf{p}\|$ into two parts.

nodes.name: First part from Step (iii)
nodes.statement: The first part, $\| p_\kappa - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\| $ is bounded in \eqref{eq:P_q_dist_bound}.
nodes.statement_short: The first part is bounded in Step (iii).

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 10.23
nodes.statement:
Furthermore, assuming event $A_\kappa$ holds, since $\alpha = \alpha_0 2^{-\kappa}<1/D$, there is $N_3$ such that for $n>N_{3}$ we have from Lemma \ref{lem:dist_to_f_l0_srtong_small_alpha} that  
	\[
	\|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq 8 \sigma D \alpha_1^2 2^{-2\kappa} + \frac{c\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)}{n^{r_0}}
	\]
	holds with probability at least $1-\delta/(\kappa+1)$, where $c$ is some general constant and $ r_0 = \frac{k}{2k +d}$. Explicitly. 
	Denote this event by~$B$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 10.23 bounds $\|\hat p_n-p_\kappa\|$ on an event $B$.

nodes.name: Substitute kappa
nodes.statement:
Substituting $\kappa$ from \eqref{eq:kappa_res_lem} we have from Lemma \ref{lem:comute_kappa} that 
	\[
	\| \hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq 8\sigma D C_{d}^2 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)^2 n^{-2r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{4r_1} + c\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)n^{-r_0}
	\]
	or, for $n$ large enough, and some constant $ C_1$,
	\begin{equation} \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq C_1 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_0}.
	\end{equation}
	Note that $p_\kappa \in \mathcal{M}$, so $dist(\hat p_n,\mathcal{M}) \leq \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \|$.
nodes.statement_short: Substitute $\kappa$ to get $\|\hat p_n-p_\kappa\|\le C_1\ln(1/\delta)n^{-r_0}$, which bounds the distance to $\mathcal{M}$.

nodes.name: Combine the two parts
nodes.statement:
Combining this with \eqref{eq:P_q_dist_bound}, assuming events $A_0,\ldots A_\kappa,B$ hold, we have that 
	\[
	\| \hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\|  \leq  C_1 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_0} + \frac{\hat C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\left(\frac{1}{2\sigma(2+\sigma/\tau)}-\frac{c}{\tau} \right)}.
	\] 
	Alternatively, for $n$ large enough, and some constant $C$, given the events $A_1,\ldots, A_\kappa, B$ hold, 
	\begin{equation} \|\hat p_n - \mathrm{\mathbf{p}}\| \leq C\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}  \left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}.    
	\end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Combine to bound $\|\hat p_n-\mathbf{p}\|$.

nodes.name: Final union bound
nodes.statement:
Using the union bound on $A_1,\ldots, A_\kappa, B$, we have that Equations \eqref{eq:res_thm33_tang}, \eqref{eq:pnhat-pkappa_bound} and \eqref{eq:pn-p_bound} are satisfied with probability of at least $1 - \delta$.
	This concludes the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:Step2}.
nodes.statement_short: Union bound gives all three estimates w.p. $\ge1-\delta$.

nodes.name: Sample size condition relating kappa and delta_1
nodes.statement: 12\sqrt{d}\frac{C_0 \ln(1/\delta_1)}{n^{r_1}} \leq \alpha_0 2^{-\kappa+1},
nodes.label: eq:n_bound1

nodes.name: Distance of p to p_kappa
nodes.statement: \|\mathrm{\mathbf{p}} - p_{\kappa}\| \leq \frac{\hat C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\left(\frac{1}{2\sigma(2+\sigma/\tau)}-\frac{c}{\tau} \right)},

nodes.name: Combined tangent angle bound
nodes.statement:
\angle_{\max}(T_{\mathbf{p}}\mathcal{M},Tf_\kappa(0))
		\leq \frac{2\hat C_{d}\ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\tau\left(\frac{1}{2\sigma(2+\sigma/\tau)}-\frac{c}{\tau} \right)} = 
		\frac{2\hat C_{d}\ln\left(
			\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_1}\left(\ln\left(\ln(n) \right)\right)^{2r_1}}{\frac{M}{4 + 2/M} -c} 
		,
nodes.label: eq:TPM_Tfk_full

nodes.name: Final tangent error
nodes.statement: \angle_{\max}(T_{\mathbf{p}}\mathcal{M},H_\kappa) \leq C_d \cdot \ln(1/\delta)n^{-r_1} (\ln \ln(n))^{2 r_1}

nodes.statement: \|\hat p_n - p_\kappa \| \leq C_1 \ln\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right) n^{-r_0}.

nodes.name: Geodesic tracking on a sampled manifold
nodes.statement:
We assume that a point $x_0$ is chosen on the manifold and some direction $\vec v_0$ on the tangent $T_{x_0} \mathcal{M}$ (In practice, the process can initialized with a point near the manifold $\mathcal{M}$ and then project it to the manifold). 

The process of tracking a geodesic line is iterative. 
At each step, we compute $\wtilde x_{i+1} =  x_i + \varepsilon \vec{v}$, then ``project'' the new point back to the manifold $x_{i+1} \approx \mbox{Proj}_{\mathcal{M}} \wtilde x_{i+1}$ through Algorithms \ref{alg:step1Inpractice_clean} and \ref{alg:step2InPractice_clean}, and parallel transport $\vec v_i$ to $T_{x_{i+1}}$ to get $\vec v_{i+1}$.
input: a point $x_0$ is chosen on the manifold and some direction $\vec v_0$ on the tangent $T_{x_0} \mathcal{M}$
nodes.statement_short: Trace a geodesic by repeatedly stepping along the current direction, projecting back to the manifold with Algorithms 3 and 4, and parallel transporting the direction.

nodes.name: Step along direction
nodes.statement: we compute $\wtilde x_{i+1} =  x_i + \varepsilon \vec{v}$

nodes.name: Project back to the manifold
nodes.statement: ``project'' the new point back to the manifold $x_{i+1} \approx \mbox{Proj}_{\mathcal{M}} \wtilde x_{i+1}$ through Algorithms \ref{alg:step1Inpractice_clean} and \ref{alg:step2InPractice_clean}
nodes.statement_short: Project the stepped point onto the manifold with Algorithms 3 and 4.

nodes.name: Parallel transport the direction
nodes.statement: parallel transport $\vec v_i$ to $T_{x_{i+1}}$ to get $\vec v_{i+1}$

nodes.name: Geodesic walk on a circle
nodes.statement:
In the first toy case, the manifold $\mathcal{M}$ is a circle of radius 10 in $\mathbb{R}^2$. 
The dataset consists of 5000 points. 
We start with some sample (illustrated in red in Figure \ref{fig:geoWalk_circle}), project it onto the circle (in Figure \ref{fig:geoWalk_circle}, the circle is marked in blue, and the projected point in green), and than move the point in some direction, project it again (shown in another green point in Figure \ref{fig:geoWalk_circle}), etc.

nodes.name: Rotating airplane image manifold
nodes.statement:
In the second example, we took a 3d model of an airplane\footnote{\textcolor{blue}{\href{http://3dmag.org/en/market/download/item/4740/}{http://3dmag.org/en/market/download/item/4740/}}}, rotated it in the z-axis, and took 2000 snapshots. Each snapshot is an image of $290 \times 209$ gray-scale pixels. The input data set consist of the unsorted images, sampled from a one dimensional manifold embedded in $\mathbb{R}^{60,610}$.
Several such images appear in Figure \ref{fig:geoWalk_airplane}. 
Starting from some image, we create a movie of the rotating airplane.

nodes.name: Bounding Ball
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with reach $\tau$. For any $p \in \mathcal{M}$, let $T_{p}\mathcal{M}$ be the tangent of $\mathcal{M}$ at $p$.
    For any $x = p + x_T$, where $x_T\in T_p\mathcal{M}$, and $y\in (T_p\mathcal{M})^\perp$  such that $\|x_T\|\leq \tau$, $\|y\| \leq \tau/2$ and $(x + y)\in \mathcal{M}$, we have that 
    \[
    \norm{y} \leq \tau-\sqrt{\tau^2-\norm{x_T}^2}
    \]

nodes.name: Bounding Ball From a Tilted Plane
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with reach $\tau$. For any $p \in \mathcal{M}$, let $T_{p}\mathcal{M}$ be the tangent of $\mathcal{M}$ at $p$ and let $ H\in Gr(d, D) $ such that $ \angle_{\max}(T_p\mathcal{M}, H) = \alpha \leq \pi/4 $.
    For any $x = p + x_H$, where $x_H\in H$, $\|x_H\|\leq c_{\pi/4}\tau$ for some constant $c_{\pi/4}$ , and $y\in H^\perp$  such that $\|x-p\|\leq \tau \cos \alpha$, $\|y\| \leq \tau/2$ and $(x + y)\in \mathcal{M}$, we have that 
	\[
	-\tau\cos\alpha+\sqrt{\tau^2-(\norm{x} - \tau\sin\alpha)^2} \leq \|y\| \leq \tau\cos\alpha-\sqrt{\tau^2-(\norm{x} + \tau\sin\alpha)^2}
	\]

nodes.name: Tangent variation along the manifold
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with reach $\tau$. For any $p \in \mathcal{M}$, let $T_{p}\mathcal{M}$ be the tangent of $\mathcal{M}$ at $p$ and let $ H\in Gr(d, D) $ such that $ \angle_{\max}(T_p\mathcal{M}, H) = \alpha\leq \pi/4 $.
	For any $x = p + x_H$, where $x_H\in H$,$\|x_H\|\leq c_{\pi/4}\tau$ for some constant $c_{\pi/4}$, and $y\in H^\perp$  such that $\|x-p\|\leq \tau \cos \alpha$, $\|y\| \leq \tau/2$ and $(x + y)\in \mathcal{M}$.

nodes.name: Angle of tangent to a tilted plane along the manifold
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with reach $\tau$. For any $p \in \mathcal{M}$, let $T_{p}\mathcal{M}$ be the tangent of $\mathcal{M}$ at $p$ and let $ H\in Gr(d, D) $ such that $ \angle_{\max}(T_p\mathcal{M}, H) = \alpha\leq \pi/4 $.
	For any $x = p + x_H$, where $x_H\in H$,$\|x_H\|\leq c_{\pi/4}\tau$ for some constant $c_{\pi/4}$, and $y\in H^\perp$  such that $\|x-p\|\leq \tau \cos \alpha$, $\|y\| \leq \tau/2$ and $(x + y)\in \mathcal{M}$, we denote $ \beta = \angle_{\max}(T_{x+y}\mathcal{M}, H) $.
	Then, we get that
        \[
      \alpha- 2\frac{\norm{x_H}}{\tau}(1 + \alpha)  +c\|x_H\|^2/\tau^2 \leq \beta \leq \alpha+ 2\frac{\norm{x_H}}{\tau}(1 + \alpha)  +c\|x_H\|^2/\tau^2
	 ,\]
  for some constant $c\in \mathbb{R}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.11
nodes.statement:
Using the triangle inequality for maximal angles we have that 
	\[
	\angle_{\max}(T_p \mathcal{M}, H) \leq \angle_{\max}(T_p \mathcal{M},T_{x+y} \mathcal{M})+\angle_{\max}(T_{x+y} \mathcal{M},H),\]
 as well as
	\[ \angle_{\max}(T_{x+y} \mathcal{M},H)
	 \leq \angle_{\max}(T_p \mathcal{M},T_{x+y} \mathcal{M})+
  \angle_{\max}(T_p \mathcal{M}, H),\]

 which can be written as 
	\[
	|\alpha - \beta| \leq \angle_{\max}(T_{x+y} \mathcal{M}, T_p \mathcal{M})
	.\]
	From Lemma~\ref{lem:alpha-beta_x_no_func} we have that 
	\[
	\sin(\angle_{\max} (T_{x+y}\mathcal{M}, T_{p}\mathcal{M})) \leq \frac{\norm{x_H}}{\tau}(1 + \tan^2 \alpha)  +\mathcal{O}(\|x_H\|^2/\tau^2)
	,\]
	and thus, 
	\[
	\sin(|\alpha - \beta|) \leq \frac{\norm{x_H}}{\tau}(1 + \tan^2 \alpha)  +\mathcal{O}(\|x_H\|^2/\tau^2)
	\]
	Since for $x\leq \pi/2$, we have that $x/2<\sin(x)$, we have 
	
	\[
	|\alpha - \beta| \leq 2\frac{\norm{x_H}}{\tau}(1 + \tan^2 \alpha)  +\mathcal{O}(\|x_H\|^2/\tau^2)
	.\]
	Since for $\alpha \leq \pi/4$, we have that $\tan \alpha \leq 1$, and $\tan^2\alpha \leq \alpha$, we have that 
    \[
      \alpha- 2\frac{\norm{x_H}}{\tau}(1 + \alpha)  +\mathcal{O}(\|x_H\|^2/\tau^2) \leq \beta \leq \alpha+ 2\frac{\norm{x_H}}{\tau}(1 + \alpha)  +\mathcal{O}(\|x_H\|^2/\tau^2)
	.\]

nodes.name: M is locally a function graph over a tilted plane
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with reach $\tau$. For any $p \in \mathcal{M}$, let $T_{p}\mathcal{M}$ be the tangent of $\mathcal{M}$ at $p$. Let $H \in Gr(d,D)$, such that $\angle_{\max}(H,T_p\mathcal{M}) = \alpha \leq \pi/4$.  
Then $\mathcal{M} \cap \emph{Cyl}_H(p,\rho, \tau/2)$ is locally a function over $H$, where $\emph{Cyl}_H(p,\rho, \tau/2)$ is the $D$-dimensional cylinder with the base $B_H(p, \rho)\subset H$ and height $\tau/2$ in any direction on $H^\perp$, for $\rho = c_{\pi/4}\tau$ where $c_{\pi/4}$ is some general constant. 

\noindent Explicitly, there exists a function 
$$
f:B_H(p, \rho) \to H^\perp
$$
such that the graph of $f$ defined as
$$
\Gamma_f = \{p + (x,f(x)) | x\in B_H(p, \rho) \} 
$$
identifies with $\mathcal{M} \cap \emph{Cyl}_H(p,\rho, \tau/2)$.

assumptions: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with reach $\tau$.
Let $H \in Gr(d,D)$, such that $\angle_{\max}(H,T_p\mathcal{M}) = \alpha \leq \pi/4$.
conclusions: Then $\mathcal{M} \cap \emph{Cyl}_H(p,\rho, \tau/2)$ is locally a function over $H$
nodes.statement_short: Within a cylinder of radius $c_{\pi/4}\tau$ over a plane tilted by at most $\pi/4$, the manifold is the graph of a single-valued function.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 8.12
nodes.statement:
We split our arguments to two separate parts.
First, we show that for $c < 0.02$ there exists a function $f$ such that $\Gamma_f \subset \mathcal{M}\cap \textrm{Cyl}_H(p,  c \tau, \tau/2)$.
Then, in the second part of the proof, we show that there is a constant $c_{\pi/4} < c$ such that $f$ is defined uniquely and $\Gamma_f = M\cap \textrm{Cyl}_H(p, \rho, \tau/2)$.

By definition, there is an open ball $U_T\subset T_p\mathcal{M}$ of $p$ such that there is a neighborhood $W_{\mathcal{M}} \subset \mathcal{M}$ that can be written as a graph of a function from $U_T\simeq \mathbb{R}^d$ to $T_p\mathcal{M}^\perp\simeq \mathbb{R}^{D-d}$.
Accordingly, for any $H$ such that $\angle_{\max}(H, T_p\mathcal{M}) < \pi/2$ there is an open ball $B_H(p,\varepsilon) \subset H$ such that $W_H \subset \mathcal{M}$ can be written as a graph of a function $f$  from $B_H(p,\varepsilon)$ to $H^\perp$.
We wish to show that $f$ can be extended to a ball $B_H(p, 0.02 \tau)\subset H$ such that the graph of $f$ is a subset of $\mathcal{M}$ (note that $f(0) = 0$).

By contradiction, let us assume that $\frak{r}$ the maximal radius of an open ball such that the $\Gamma_f \subset \mathcal{M}$, is strictly smaller than $0.02 \tau$.
We claim that the graph $\Gamma_f$ is defined on the closed ball $\bar B_H(p, \frak{r})$ and is also subset of $\mathcal{M}$.
This is true, from the following argument:
Take a sequence of points $\{x_n\}$ converging to $ x\in \partial \bar B_H(p, \frak{r})$, a point on the boundary of $\bar B_H(p, \rho)$, and consider $\{y_n = p + (x_n, f(x_n))\in \mathcal{M}\}$. From the compactness of $\mathcal{M}$ the sequence $y_n$ has a converging subsequence $y_{n_k}$ and we denote its limit as $y$.
Since $x_n \to x$, we define $f(x)\stackrel{\bigtriangleup}{=}\lim f(x_{n_k})$ and  $y = p + (x, f(x))$.

We now wish to show that there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that $f$ can be extended to $B_H(p, \frak{r} + \varepsilon)$.
Using a similar argument to the one used in the beginning of the proof, by showing that for any $x\in\partial B_H(p, \frak{r})$ the angle $\angle_{\max}(T_x f, H) < \pi/2$, we get that there is $W_H\subset\mathcal{M}$, a neighborhood of $y\in \mathcal{M}$ that is the image of some function from $B_H(x,\varepsilon_x)$ to $H^\perp$.
Therefore, $f$ can be extended into this neighborhood.
Taking $\varepsilon$ to be the minimum over all $\varepsilon_x$, which exists since $x$ is in $H(p, \frak{r})$, which is compact, we get that $f$ can be extended to $B_H(p, \frak{r}+ \varepsilon)$.

The remaining piece of the existence puzzle is showing that for all $x\in\partial B_H(p, \frak{r})$ we have $\angle_{\max}(T_x f, H) < \pi/2$.
From Lemma \ref{lem:alpha_beta_x_no_func} we have that for any $x$ such that 
\[
       \frac{\pi}{2} \leq \frac{\pi}{4}+ 2\frac{\norm{x}}{\tau}(1 + \frac{\pi}{4})  +c\|x\|^2/\tau^2
	 .\]




$\angle_{\max}(T_xf,H) <\pi/2$ holds.
Rewriting the inequality we get
\[
\begin{array}{cc}
      \\
    \frac{\pi}{4} > & 2\frac{\norm{x}}{\tau}(1 + \frac{\pi}{4})  +c\|x\|^2/\tau^2\\
    0 > & c\frac{\norm{x}^2}{\tau^2} +  \frac{\norm{x}}{\tau} (1 + \frac{\pi}{4}) - \frac{\pi}{8},\\
\end{array}
\]
Thus, for $x< c_1 \tau$ we have that  $\angle_{\max}(T_xf,H) <\pi/2$ holds.


We now turn to show that there is a constant $c_{\pi/4}$ for which $f$ is uniquely defined in $B_H(p, c_{\pi/4}\tau)$.
From Lemma \ref{lem:f_bound_circle_H_no_func_clean} we know that for any $x \in H$ with $\|x\|\leq \tau/2$ all the $y\in H^\perp$ such that $(x,y)\in\mathcal{M}$ and $\|y\| \leq \tau/2$ must satisfy:
\begin{equation}
    \|y\| \leq \tau\cos\alpha-\sqrt{\tau^2-(\norm{x} + \tau\sin\alpha)^2} = \tau\left(\cos\alpha-\sqrt{1-(\frac{\norm{x}}{\tau} + \sin\alpha)^2}\right)
\end{equation}
Let $y_1, y_2$ be such that $(x,y_1),(x,y_2)\in\mathcal{M}$ where $\norm{x}=\bar x\tau$.
Then,
\begin{equation}
    \|y_j\| \leq \tau\left(\cos\alpha-\sqrt{1-(\bar x+ \sin\alpha)^2}\right),\quad (j=1,2)
.\end{equation}
In other words, $y_1$ and $y_2$ cannot be too far from one another, and note that as $\bar x \to 0$
\begin{equation} \norm{y_2 - y_1} \to 0
\end{equation}

On the other hand, taking the point $(x, y_1)\in \mathcal{M}$, denoting $\beta = \angle_{\max} (T_{(x, y_1)}\mathcal{M}, H)$, and applying Lemma \ref{lem:alpha_beta_x_no_func} we have that
\[
\beta \leq \alpha+ 2\frac{\bar x}{\tau}(1 + \alpha)  +\mathcal{O}(\bar x^2/\tau^2)
\]




which tends to $\alpha$ when $\bar x\to 0$.
From Lemma \ref{lem:reach_ball_no_intersect_clean} we know that $(x,y_2)$ cannot be in any ball tangent to $\mathcal{M}$ at $(x, y_1)$ of radius $\tau$.
We denote by $v$ the direction $(0, y_2 - y_1)\in H^\perp$. 
From Lemma \ref{lem:angle_space_to_vec}  we know that there is $w \in \lrbrackets{ T_{(x, y_1)} \mathcal{M}} ^\perp$ such that $\angle (v, w) \leq \beta$.
Therefore, we can now limit our discussion to $L_{y_1}$ the affine space spanned by $v$ and $w$ from $(x, y_1)$, and note that it contains $(x, y_2)$ as well.
Taking the two balls $B_D((x, y_1) \pm \tau\cdot w, \tau)$ and intersecting them with $L_{y_1}$ we get two 2-dimensional disks of radius $\tau$ (see Figure \ref{fig:bouding_balls_for lem_locally_func}).
Thus, $(x, y_2)$ cannot be within either disks.
From basic trigonometry we achieve that either $y_2 = y_1$ or
\[
\norm{y_2 - y_1} \geq 2\tau\cos(\beta) \geq 2\tau\cos(\alpha + 2\sqrt{\bar x (2\alpha + \bar x)})
,\]
which tends to $2\tau \cos \alpha$ as $\bar x \to 0$.
Combining this with \eqref{eq:y2_y1_diff} we get there is $c_{\pi/4}$  such that for all $\bar x \leq c_{\pi/4}$ we have $y_1 = y_2$.
\begin{figure}[htb!]
    \centering
    \includegraphics
 [width=0.45\textwidth]{Figures/BoundingCircle_Twicev2.pdf}
    \caption{Illustration of bounding balls. The reach $\tau$ of the manifold $\mathcal{M}$ (marked by the red line) bounds its sectional curvatures. Namely, the manifold cannot intersect a tangent open ball of radius $\tau$. In this illustration we have some coordinate system $H$ and the manifold can be described locally as a graph of some function $f:H\to H^\perp$. The coordinate system $H$ is not aligned with $T_0f$, the tangent at zero; i.e., $\angle_{\max}(H, T_0f) = \alpha$. Then the value of $f$ at $x$ is bounded to the markered interval in $H^\perp$ above $x$. Furthermore, in order to have two different points in $\mathcal{M}$ above $x$, the manifold cannot curve too fast as it cannot enter neither the dotted balls nor the solid ones.} \end{figure}

\begin{equation}
    \|y_j\| \leq \tau\left(\cos\alpha-\sqrt{1-(\bar x+ \sin\alpha)^2}\right),\quad (j=1,2)
.\end{equation}
In other words, $y_1$ and $y_2$ cannot be too far from one another, and note that as $\bar x \to 0$
\begin{equation} \norm{y_2 - y_1} \to 0
\end{equation}

On the other hand, taking the point $(x, y_1)\in \mathcal{M}$, denoting $\beta = \angle_{\max} (T_{(x, y_1)}\mathcal{M}, H)$, and applying Lemma \ref{lem:alpha_beta_x_no_func} we have that
\[
\beta \leq \alpha+ 2\frac{\bar x}{\tau}(1 + \alpha)  +\mathcal{O}(\bar x^2/\tau^2)
\]




which tends to $\alpha$ when $\bar x\to 0$.
From Lemma \ref{lem:reach_ball_no_intersect_clean} we know that $(x,y_2)$ cannot be in any ball tangent to $\mathcal{M}$ at $(x, y_1)$ of radius $\tau$.
We denote by $v$ the direction $(0, y_2 - y_1)\in H^\perp$. 
From Lemma \ref{lem:angle_space_to_vec}  we know that there is $w \in \lrbrackets{ T_{(x, y_1)} \mathcal{M}} ^\perp$ such that $\angle (v, w) \leq \beta$.
Therefore, we can now limit our discussion to $L_{y_1}$ the affine space spanned by $v$ and $w$ from $(x, y_1)$, and note that it contains $(x, y_2)$ as well.
Taking the two balls $B_D((x, y_1) \pm \tau\cdot w, \tau)$ and intersecting them with $L_{y_1}$ we get two 2-dimensional disks of radius $\tau$ (see Figure \ref{fig:bouding_balls_for lem_locally_func}).
Thus, $(x, y_2)$ cannot be within either disks.
From basic trigonometry we achieve that either $y_2 = y_1$ or
\[
\norm{y_2 - y_1} \geq 2\tau\cos(\beta) \geq 2\tau\cos(\alpha + 2\sqrt{\bar x (2\alpha + \bar x)})
,\]
which tends to $2\tau \cos \alpha$ as $\bar x \to 0$.
Combining this with \eqref{eq:y2_y1_diff} we get there is $c_{\pi/4}$  such that for all $\bar x \leq c_{\pi/4}$ we have $y_1 = y_2$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.1
nodes.statement:
We recall that $ U_\textrm{ROI} $ as defined in \eqref{eq:ROI_clean} is contained in $ B_D({p_r}, \sqrt{\sigma\tau} + \sigma) $.
Using Lemma \ref{lem:dist_ri_TpM_clean}, for any $r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}$ we know that the distance between $r_i - p_r$ and $ T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M} $ is bounded by 
\begin{equation} \operatorname{dist}(r_i - p_r,T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) \leq \tau-\sqrt{\tau^2-\|x_i\|^2}  + \sigma
,\end{equation}
where $ x_i = Proj_{T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}}(r_i - p_r) $.
Since $ x_i \in B_D(0, \sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma )$ we have that $\norm{x_i} \leq \sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma $, and so
\[
J_1(r; {p_r}, T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) \leq \left(\tau-\sqrt{\tau^2-(\sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma)^2} + \sigma\right)^2 
.\]
By simplifying and bounding this expression using Remark \ref{rem:taylor2_sqrt1-x2_clean} we get
	\begin{align*}
		\left((\sigma+\tau)-\sqrt{\tau^2-(\sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma)^2}\right)^2 = & (\sigma+\tau)^2 + \tau^2-(\sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma)^2 - 2(\sigma+\tau) \sqrt{\tau^2-(\sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma)^2}\\
		= &
		\sigma^2 + 2\sigma\tau + 2 \tau^2 -  (\sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma)^2 \\
		&- 2\tau(\sigma+\tau) \sqrt{1-(\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^2}\\
		\leq &
		\sigma^2 + 2\sigma\tau + 2 \tau^2 - (\sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma)^2\\
		& - 2\tau^2 (1-1/2 (\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^2- (\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^4 )\\& - 2\tau\sigma (1-1/2 (\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^2- (\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^4)\\
		= &
		\sigma^2 -  \tau^2(\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^2 \\
		& + \tau^2  ((\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^2  +2(\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^4) \\& + \tau\sigma  ((\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^2+2(\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^4) \\
		= &
		\sigma^2 + 2\tau^2 (\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^4\\& + \tau\sigma ( (\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^2 +2(\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}+\sigma/\tau)^4)\\
		\leq &
		\sigma^2 + 2 \left(\sqrt{\sigma} + \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right)^4
		+ 3\sigma
		\left(\sqrt{\sigma} + \frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{\tau}}\right)^2 
	.\end{align*}
Using the fact that $ \sigma \leq \tau $ we get
\begin{align*}
J_1(r; {p_r}, T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) &\leq
\sigma^2 + 2(2\sqrt{\sigma})^4 + 3\sigma (2\sqrt{\sigma})^2
\end{align*}
Thus, we obtain
$$J_1(r; {p_r}, T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) \leq 49 \sigma^2.$$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement:
We first wish to denote by $\beta_j$ the principal angles between $H$ and $T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}$ and their matching principal pairs $(u_j, w_j)\in T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}\times H$ (see Definition \ref{def:principal_angles_clean}).
