Thus, we can define the orthogonal complement of $u_j$ and $w_j$ on $\mathcal{L}_j$ by $y_j$ and $\tilde y_j$ correspondingly.
That is, both $\{u_j, y_j\}$ and $\{w_j, \tilde y_j\}$ are orthogonal bases of $\mathcal{L}_j$.
Since for any $i \neq j$ we have that $u_i \perp w_j$, $u_i \perp u_j$ and $w_i \perp w_j$, we have that both $\{\tilde y_j\}_{j=1}^{d}$ and $\{y_j\}_{j=1}^{d}$ are orthonormal sets.
Then, complete the sets $\{\tilde y_j\}_{j=1}^{d}$ and $\{y_j\}_{j=1}^{d}$  to an orthonormal basis of $H^\perp$  and $T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}^\perp$ through adding the orthonormal sets $\{\tilde y_j\}_{j=d+1}^{D-d}$ and $\{y_j\}_{j=d+1}^{D-d}$ correspondingly. Note that, since $H^\perp$ is a $D-d$ dimensional space, and $\{\wtilde y_j\}_{j=1}^{d} \in H^\perp$, we need only to add $D-2d$ vectors to have an orthonormal basis.
Explicitly, we know that for all $j' = 1\ldots, d$
$$\textrm{Span}\{\tilde y_j\}_{j=d+1}^{D-d}\perp \mathcal{L}_{j'} ~~,~~ \textrm{Span}\{ y_j\}_{j=d+1}^{D-d}\perp \mathcal{L}_{j'}.$$ 
Thus, for $j=d+1, \ldots, D-d$ we have both $\tilde y_j , y_j\in H^\perp \cap T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}^\perp$ and without limiting the generality we can choose $\tilde y_j = y_j$ for such $j$.
Using this notation we get that for any point $x\in U_\textrm{ROI}$
\[
\operatorname{dist}^2(x - {p_r}, H) = 
\sum_{j=1}^{D-d} \lrangle{x - {p_r}, \tilde y_j}^2 =
\sum_{j=1}^{D-d} \lrangle{x - {p_r}, \tilde y_j}^2 + \sum_{j=1}^{D-d} \left[\lrangle{x - {p_r},  y_j}^2 - \lrangle{x - {p_r},  y_j}^2\right] =
\]
\[
=\sum_{j=1}^{D-d} \lrangle{x - {p_r}, y_j}^2 + \sum_{j=1}^{D-d}\left[ \lrangle{x - {p_r},  \tilde y_j}^2 - \lrangle{x - {p_r},  y_j}^2\right]
,\]
and since $\tilde y_j = y_j$ for $j=d+1,\ldots,D-d$ we have
\begin{align} \operatorname{dist}^2(x - {p_r}, H) &=
	\operatorname{dist}^2(x - {p_r}, T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) + \sum_{j=1}^{d}\left[ \langle x - {p_r}, \tilde{y}_j \rangle^2 - \langle x - {p_r}, {y}_j \rangle^2\right]
.\end{align}

The remainder of the proof is achieved through the following set of claims:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item From \eqref{eq:EJ_1_clean} it follows that
    \[J_1(r; {p_r}, H) =  J_1(r;{p_r},T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}) +  R_1(r;{p_r},H),\]
    where
    \begin{equation} R_1(r; {p_r}, H) = \sum\limits_{j=1}^{d} \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}}  \langle r_i - {p_r}, \tilde{y}_j \rangle^2 - \langle r_i - {p_r}, {y}_j \rangle^2
    .\end{equation}
    \item Thus, in order to bound $J_1(r; {p_r}, H)$ from below we can focus on bounding $R_1(r; {p_r}, H)$.
    We then consider separately two sets of indices $\mathcal{K}', \mathcal{K}''$ such that $\mathcal{K}' \cup \mathcal{K}'' = \{1,\ldots, d\}$, where for all $j\in \mathcal{K}'$ we have $\beta_j > \alpha$ and for all $j\in \mathcal{K}''$ we have $\beta_j\leq \alpha$.
    Notice that since $\angle_{max}(H, T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}) > \alpha$ we, get that $\mathcal{K}' \not = \emptyset$ and that $\#\mathcal{K}'' \leq d-1$.
    Writing this explicitly we get
    \begin{equation} R_1(r; {p_r}, H) = R_1'(r; {p_r}, H)  +  R_1''(r; {p_r}, H)
    \end{equation}
    where 
    \begin{equation} R_1'(r; {p_r}, H) = \sum\limits_{j\in\mathcal{K}'} \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}}  \langle r_i - {p_r}, \tilde{y}_j \rangle^2 - \langle r_i - {p_r}, {y}_j \rangle^2
    ,\end{equation}
    and
    \begin{equation} R_1''(r; {p_r}, H) = \sum\limits_{j\in\mathcal{K}''} \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}}  \langle r_i - {p_r}, \tilde{y}_j \rangle^2 - \langle r_i - {p_r}, {y}_j \rangle^2
    .\end{equation}
    \item We show in Section \ref{sec:proof_claim_R1pp_bound_clean} that
    \begin{equation} R_1''(r; {p_r}, H) \geq
    -9 \sigma^2
    .\end{equation}
    \item Then, when we focus on $j\in\mathcal{K}'$ we show that for $a_1 = \frac{1}{4}$ and $a_2 = \frac{1}{8}$ and $x_0\in T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}$ such that $\norm{{p_r} - x_0} = a_1\sqrt{\sigma\tau}$ and $B_{T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2 \sqrt{\sigma\tau} + \sigma)\subset B_D({p_r}, \sqrt{\sigma \tau} - \sigma) \subset U_\textrm{ROI}$, and 
    \begin{equation} \lrangle{r_i - {p_r}, \tilde y_j}^2 \geq \frac{1}{64}\sigma \tau sin\alpha - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2}
    .\end{equation}
    This is proven in \ref{subsec:proof_lem_ri_tyk_bound_clean}.
    \item From Assumption \ref{assume:noise} in Section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions} we know that $ \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} < \frac{1}{2} $. 
    In addition, setting $ \rho = a_2 \sqrt{\sigma \tau} $ we know that $ B_{T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho+\sigma)\subset B_{T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}}({p_r}, \sqrt{\sigma \tau} - \sigma) $, so we can use Lemma \ref{lem:num_of_samples_in_a_ball_clean}.
    Explicitly, let $\mathrm{V}_d = \frac{\pi^{d/2}}{\Gamma(d/2+1)}$ be the volume of a $ d $-dimensional unit ball, and denote 
     \begin{align*}
    \mu_{\min} &= \mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d} \min_{\substack{p\in \mathcal{M}\\ x\in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(0,\sqrt{\sigma\tau}- \sigma)}}  \sqrt{det(G_p(x))}\\
    \mu_{\max} &= \mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d}\max_{\substack{p\in \mathcal{M} \\ x \in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(0,\sqrt{\sigma\tau}- \sigma)}}  \sqrt{det(G_p(x))}
    ,
    \end{align*}
    where $ \mathrm{Vol}(B_{{T_p\mathcal{M}}^\perp}(\sigma)) $ is the volume of a $ D-d $ dimensional ball with radius $ \sigma $ and $ G_p $ is the matrix representing the Riemannian metric at $ p $ in the chart $ \varphi_p $ of \eqref{eq:phi_def_clean}.
    Then, from Lemma \ref{lem:num_of_samples_in_a_ball_clean}, we get that for any $ \varepsilon, \delta $ there is $ N $ such that for all $ n > N $
    \begin{align*}
    &\#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0,\rho) \}
    \leq
    n(2\cdot \mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d+\varepsilon) \\
    &\#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0,\rho+\sigma) \}
    \geq
    n \left(\frac{\mu_{max}}{2}\cdot \mathrm{V}_{d}\cdot \rho^d - \varepsilon\right)
    \end{align*}
    with probability of at least $1-\delta$.
    By setting $ \varepsilon $ appropriately we get 
    \begin{align*}
    &\#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0,\rho) \}
    \leq
    3 n \cdot\mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d \\
    &\#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0,\rho+\sigma) \}
    \geq
    \frac{n}{3}  \cdot\mu_{max}\cdot \mathrm{V}_{d} \cdot \rho^d 
    .\end{align*}
    \item Rephrasing \ref{thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean}-\ref{thm:claim_useStochasticLemma} as one statement, there is a large subset of $U_\textrm{ROI}$ with large values of $\lrangle{r_i - p, \tilde y_j}^2$, with probability of at least $1-\delta$.
    Accordingly, we show that for any $ \delta $ there is $ N_\delta $ such that for all $ n>N_\delta $ 
    \begin{align}
    R_1'(r; p, H) \geq  &\frac{\mu_{max}}{\mu_{min} }\cdot\frac{1}{9} \left(\frac{1-\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}}{ 8}\right)^d\cdot \left(\frac{1}{64}\sigma \tau sin\alpha - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2} \right)  -9 \sigma^2 ,\end{align}
    with probability of at least $1-\delta$.
    This is proven in \ref{subsec:proof_lem_R1p_bound_clean}.
    
    \item Combining \eqref{eq:RpRpp_clean} with \eqref{eq:R1pp_bound_clean} and \eqref{eq:R1p_bound_clean}, we get that for $\alpha = \sqrt{C_{M}/M}$, where $M = \frac{\tau}{\sigma}$, and $C_{M}$ is a constant the following holds:
    For any $ \delta > 0$ there is $ N $ such that for all $ n > N $
    \begin{equation}
        R_1(r;p,H) \geq 109 \sigma^2
    ,\end{equation}
    with probability of at least $1-\delta$.
    \item From Claim \ref{thm:claim_J1H_clean} above, since $J_1(r;{p_r},T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}) \geq 0$ we achieve that with probability of at least $1-\delta$ there is $N_\delta$ large enough such that for all $ n > N_\delta $ we have
$
       J_1(r; p, H) \geq 109 \sigma^2  
    ,$
    as required.
    
\end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Decompose the score in principal-angle coordinates into the tangent score plus a remainder $R_1$, bound the small-angle part below by $-9\sigma^2$ and the large-angle part via sample counts in a good region. The key step is the lower bound on $R_1'$ from many samples with large normal component.

nodes.name: Principal-angle bases
nodes.statement:
We first wish to denote by $\beta_j$ the principal angles between $H$ and $T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}$ and their matching principal pairs $(u_j, w_j)\in T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}\times H$ (see Definition \ref{def:principal_angles_clean}).  
Throughout the proof we work on the sectional planes defined by $\mathcal{L}_j = Span\{u_j,w_j\}$.
Thus, we can define the orthogonal complement of $u_j$ and $w_j$ on $\mathcal{L}_j$ by $y_j$ and $\tilde y_j$ correspondingly.
That is, both $\{u_j, y_j\}$ and $\{w_j, \tilde y_j\}$ are orthogonal bases of $\mathcal{L}_j$.
Since for any $i \neq j$ we have that $u_i \perp w_j$, $u_i \perp u_j$ and $w_i \perp w_j$, we have that both $\{\tilde y_j\}_{j=1}^{d}$ and $\{y_j\}_{j=1}^{d}$ are orthonormal sets.

nodes.name: Complete the bases
nodes.statement:
Then, complete the sets $\{\tilde y_j\}_{j=1}^{d}$ and $\{y_j\}_{j=1}^{d}$  to an orthonormal basis of $H^\perp$  and $T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}^\perp$ through adding the orthonormal sets $\{\tilde y_j\}_{j=d+1}^{D-d}$ and $\{y_j\}_{j=d+1}^{D-d}$ correspondingly. Note that, since $H^\perp$ is a $D-d$ dimensional space, and $\{\wtilde y_j\}_{j=1}^{d} \in H^\perp$, we need only to add $D-2d$ vectors to have an orthonormal basis.
Explicitly, we know that for all $j' = 1\ldots, d$
$$\textrm{Span}\{\tilde y_j\}_{j=d+1}^{D-d}\perp \mathcal{L}_{j'} ~~,~~ \textrm{Span}\{ y_j\}_{j=d+1}^{D-d}\perp \mathcal{L}_{j'}.$$ 
Thus, for $j=d+1, \ldots, D-d$ we have both $\tilde y_j , y_j\in H^\perp \cap T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}^\perp$ and without limiting the generality we can choose $\tilde y_j = y_j$ for such $j$.
nodes.statement_short: Complete to bases of $H^\perp$ and $T_{p_r}\mathcal{M}^\perp$ sharing the common vectors.

nodes.name: Distance decomposition
nodes.statement:
Using this notation we get that for any point $x\in U_\textrm{ROI}$
\[
\operatorname{dist}^2(x - {p_r}, H) = 
\sum_{j=1}^{D-d} \lrangle{x - {p_r}, \tilde y_j}^2 =
\sum_{j=1}^{D-d} \lrangle{x - {p_r}, \tilde y_j}^2 + \sum_{j=1}^{D-d} \left[\lrangle{x - {p_r},  y_j}^2 - \lrangle{x - {p_r},  y_j}^2\right] =
\]
\[
=\sum_{j=1}^{D-d} \lrangle{x - {p_r}, y_j}^2 + \sum_{j=1}^{D-d}\left[ \lrangle{x - {p_r},  \tilde y_j}^2 - \lrangle{x - {p_r},  y_j}^2\right]
,\]
and since $\tilde y_j = y_j$ for $j=d+1,\ldots,D-d$ we have
\begin{align} \operatorname{dist}^2(x - {p_r}, H) &=
	\operatorname{dist}^2(x - {p_r}, T_{{p_r}}\mathcal{M}) + \sum_{j=1}^{d}\left[ \langle x - {p_r}, \tilde{y}_j \rangle^2 - \langle x - {p_r}, {y}_j \rangle^2\right]
.\end{align}

The remainder of the proof is achieved through the following set of claims:
\begin{enumerate}

    We then consider separately two sets of indices $\mathcal{K}', \mathcal{K}''$ such that $\mathcal{K}' \cup \mathcal{K}'' = \{1,\ldots, d\}$, where for all $j\in \mathcal{K}'$ we have $\beta_j > \alpha$ and for all $j\in \mathcal{K}''$ we have $\beta_j\leq \alpha$.

    Writing this explicitly we get
    \begin{equation} R_1(r; {p_r}, H) = R_1'(r; {p_r}, H)  +  R_1''(r; {p_r}, H)
    \end{equation}
    where

nodes.name: Conclude

       J_1(r; p, H) \geq 109 \sigma^2

\end{enumerate}

nodes.name: Proof of Claim on R_1''
nodes.statement:
It is clear from \eqref{eq:R1pp_def_clean} that
\[
R_1''(r; p, H) \geq
- \sum\limits_{j\in\mathcal{K}''} \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}}   \langle r_i - p, {y}_j \rangle^2 =  - \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}}\sum\limits_{j\in\mathcal{K}''}\langle r_i - p, {y}_j \rangle^2
.\]
Furthermore, since $y_j\in T_p\mathcal{M}^\perp$ and by Lemma \ref{lem:dist_ri_TpM_clean} we get 
\[
\sum\limits_{j\in\mathcal{K}''}\abs{\lrangle{r_i - p, y_j}}^2 \leq dist^2(r_i - p, T_p\mathcal{M}) \leq \left(\tau - \sqrt{\tau^2 - \norm{Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i- p) }^2} + \sigma\right)^2 
,\]
and since $r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI} \subset B_D(p, \sqrt{\sigma\tau} + \sigma)$ we get
\begin{align*}
     \sum\limits_{j\in\mathcal{K}''}\langle r_i - p,y_j \rangle^2 
     & \leq 
	\left(\tau+\sigma-\sqrt{\tau^2-(\sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma)^2}\right)^2 \\
	& = \lrbrackets{\tau + \sigma - \tau\sqrt{1 - \lrbrackets{\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} + \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }^2 }}^2
\end{align*}
by Taylor expansion (Remark \ref{rem:taylor_sqrt1-x2_clean})
\begin{align*}
     \sum\limits_{j\in\mathcal{K}''}\langle r_i - p,y_j \rangle^2 
	& \leq 
	\lrbrackets{\tau + \sigma - \tau\lrbrackets{1 - \frac{1}{2}\lrbrackets{\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} + \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }^2}}^2 \\
	&=
	\lrbrackets{\sigma + \tau \frac{1}{2}\lrbrackets{\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} + \frac{\sigma}{\tau} }^2}^2 \\
\end{align*} 
since $ \sigma < \tau $ we get $\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} > \frac{\sigma}{\tau} $ and
\begin{align} \sum\limits_{j\in\mathcal{K}''}\langle r_i - p,y_j \rangle^2 
	& \leq 
	\lrbrackets{\sigma + 2\tau \frac{\sigma}{\tau}}^2 = 9 \sigma^2
\end{align}
and
\begin{equation*}
R_1''(r; p, H) \geq
-  \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}}   9 \sigma^2 =  -9 \sigma^2
\end{equation*}

nodes.name: Proof of Claim on R_1'
nodes.statement:
For all $j\in \mathcal{K}'$ we have $\beta_j>\alpha$.
Assume without loss of generality that there is only one index $\tilde j$ in $\mathcal{K}'$ (otherwise we can treat each index separately and arrive at the same conclusion), then \eqref{eq:R1p_def_clean} can be rewritten as
\[
R_1'(r; p, H) = \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}}  \langle r_i - p, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2 - \langle r_i - p, {y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2
.\]
Thus, the only property which affect the score of $R_1'$ is the difference between the measurements $\langle r_i - p, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2$ and $\langle r_i - p, {y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2$, both on the 2D plane $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$.
Accordingly, using the bisector of $\angle(\tilde y_{\tilde  j}, y_{\tilde  j})$ and its orthogonal complement, we can split $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$ into four regions $L_1, L_2, L_3, L_4$ (see Figure \ref{fig:Lk_clean}), where in two regions ($L_2$ and $L_4$ in Figure \ref{fig:Lk_clean}) $\lrangle{r_i - p, \tilde y_{\tilde j}} \geq \lrangle{r_i - p, y_{\tilde j}}$ and in the other two regions ($L_1$ and $L_3$ in Figure \ref{fig:Lk_clean}) $\lrangle{r_i - p, \tilde y_{\tilde j}} \leq \lrangle{r_i - p, y_{\tilde j}}$.
By denoting 
$$U_{bad} = \{r_i \in U_\textrm{ROI} ~|~ Proj_{\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}}(r_i - p)\in L_1 \cup L_3\},$$
and
$$U_{good} = \{r_i \in U_\textrm{ROI} ~|~ Proj_{\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}}(r_i - p)\in L_2 \cup L_4\}$$
we get that
\[
R_1'(r; p, H) = \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\left[\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_{good}}\left[  \langle r_i - p, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2 - \langle r_i - p, {y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2\right] + \sum\limits_{r_i\in U_{bad}} \left[ \langle r_i - p, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2 - \langle r_i - p, {y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2\right]\right]
\]
\[
R_1'(r; p, H) \geq \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\left[\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_{good}}  \langle r_i - p, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2 - \sum\limits_{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}} \langle r_i - p, {y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2\right]
.\]
Similar to \eqref{eq:ri_yk_bound_s_square_clean}, 
\[
\frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_\textrm{ROI}} \langle r_i - p, {y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2 \leq 9 \sigma^2
,\]
and thus
\[
R_1'(r; p, H) \geq \frac{1}{\#|U_\textrm{ROI}|}\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_{good}}  \langle r_i - p, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2
-9\sigma^2
.\]
Therefore, all we need to show is that given $n$ large enough, there are enough samples in $U_{good}$ for which the value $\lrangle{r_i - p, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}^2$ is large enough.
Using Lemma \ref{lem:num_of_samples_in_a_ball_clean}, as described in Claim \ref{thm:claim_useStochasticLemma}, since $U_\textrm{ROI}\subset B_D(Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r), \sqrt{\sigma \tau}+\sigma)$, then for any $\delta$ there is $N$ large enough such that for all $n>N$  with probability of at least $1 - \delta$ 
\[
\#|U_\textrm{ROI}| < 3n\cdot\mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_{d}\cdot (\sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma)^d 
.\]
Thus,
\[
R_1'(r; p, H) \geq \frac{1}{3n\cdot\mu_{min}\cdot V\cdot ( \sqrt{\sigma\tau} +\sigma)^d }\sum\limits_{r_i\in U_{good}}  \langle r_i - p, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle^2
-9\sigma^2
.\]
Below in the proof of Claim \ref{thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean} we show that \eqref{eq:ri_tyk_bound_clean} holds (the proof below is independent of the current one, but utilizes the notion of $U_{good}$ defined above).
Explicitly, for $ r_i \in U_{good} $
\begin{equation*}
\lrangle{r_i - p, \tilde y_j}^2 \geq \frac{1}{64}\sigma \tau \sin\alpha_0 - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2}
.\end{equation*}
Combining this with Lemma \ref{lem:num_of_samples_in_a_ball_clean} we get that for any $\delta$ there is $N$ large enough such that for all $n>N$  with probability of at least $1-\delta$
\begin{align*}
R_1'(r; p, H) 
&\geq 
\frac{\frac{n}{3}\cdot \mu_{max}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot(a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau})^d}{3n\cdot\mu_{min}\cdot V\cdot ( \sqrt{\sigma\tau}+\sigma)^d}\left(\frac{1}{64}\sigma\tau sin\alpha_0 -  \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2} \right)
-9\sigma^2 \\
&=
\frac{ a_2^d\cdot\mu_{max}}{9\cdot\mu_{min}}\left(\frac{ 1}{1+\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}}\right)^d\left(\frac{1}{64}\sigma\tau sin\alpha_0 - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2} \right)
-9 \sigma^2
.\end{align*}
Since $1/(1+x) \geq 1-x$ for sufficiently small $x$ we have that, for large enough $M$ of Assumption \ref{assume:noise}, of section \ref{sec:SamplingAssumptions},
\[
\left(\frac{ 1}{1+\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}}\right)^d \leq (1-\sqrt{\sigma/\tau})^d
\]
holds.
Thus, we have 
\[
R_1'(r; p, H) \geq \frac{ a_2^d\cdot\mu_{max}}{9\cdot\mu_{min}}(1-\sqrt{\sigma/\tau})^d\left(\frac{1}{64}\sigma\tau sin\alpha_0 - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2} \right)
-9 \sigma^2,
\]
Since $a_2 = 1/8$ we have 
\[
R_1'(r; p, H) \geq \frac{ \mu_{max}}{\mu_{min}}\cdot\frac{1}{9}\left(\frac{1-\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}}{ 8}\right)^d \left(\frac{1}{64}\sigma\tau sin\alpha_0 - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2} \right)
-9 \sigma^2,
\]
as required.


\begin{figure}[htb]
    \centering
    \includegraphics[width=0.8\textwidth]{Figures/Manifold_Good_disc4.pdf}
    \caption{Assisting illustration for the proof of Claim \ref{thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean}: the sphere section \emph{(}in purple\emph{)} represents the manifold; The $xy$-plane represents $T_p\mathcal{M}$; the plane $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$ is spanned by $y_{\tilde j}\in T_p\mathcal{M}^\perp$ and $u_{\tilde j}\in T_p\mathcal{M}$; the blue disc on $T_p\mathcal{M}$ is $B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(p, \sqrt{\sigma\tau} - \sigma)$; the manifold is considered to be the graph of the function $\phi_p:B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(p, \sqrt{\sigma\tau}- \sigma)\to T_p\mathcal{M}^\perp$. } \end{figure}

nodes.name: Proof of Claim on large normal components
nodes.statement:
As a result of Corollary \ref{cor:GraphOfFunctionTau_ROI}, $r_i \in U_\textrm{ROI}$ can be written as 
$$
r_i = \underbrace{p+(x_i, \phi_p(x_i))}_{p_i}+\varepsilon_i ,
$$
where $x_i=Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i - p)\in T_{p}\mathcal{M}$ and $\|\varepsilon_i\| \leq \sigma$.
Since 
$$ 
B_D(p, \sqrt{\sigma\tau}-\sigma ) \subset B_D(r, \sqrt{\sigma\tau}) = U_\textrm{ROI}
$$
(see the blue disc on $T_p\mathcal{M}$ in Figure \ref{fig:ManifoldGoodDisc_clean}), we look for a point $x_0\in T_p\mathcal{M}\cap \mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$ and a radius $\rho >0$ such that $\Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}^\sigma\subset B_D(p, \sqrt{\sigma\tau} - \sigma)$, where
\begin{equation}
    \Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}^\sigma \stackrel{\bigtriangleup}{=} \{x ~|~ dist(x, \Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}) < \sigma\}
,\end{equation}
where we remind that
\[
\Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)} = \{p + (x, \phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}} ~|~ x\in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)\}
.\]
Furthermore, we choose $x_0$ and $\rho$, such that $\lrangle{r_i - p, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}^2$ is large for any point $r_i\in\Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}^\sigma$ (see Figure \ref{fig:ManifoldGoodDisc_clean} for an illustration).

For convenience, we denote by $q^y, q^x, q^{\vec x}$ the projections of $q\in \Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}^\sigma$ onto $y_{\tilde j}$ (i.e., $T_p\mathcal{M}^\perp\cap \mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$), $u_{\tilde j}$ (i.e., $T_p\mathcal{M}\cap \mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$) and $T_p\mathcal{M}$ respectively.
Let $a_1, a_2<1$ and we define 
\[\rho = a_2 \cdot\sqrt{\sigma\tau}, ~~~\mbox{ and }~~~
x_0 = (a_1\sqrt{\sigma\tau})\cdot u_{\tilde j}\in T_p\mathcal{M} \cap \mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}.\]
That is, 
$
\norm{p - x_0} = a_1 \cdot \sqrt{\sigma\tau}
$.
In order to make sure that $\Gamma^\sigma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}\subset U_{\textrm{ROI}}$ we restrict the choice of $a_1, a_2$ such that
\begin{equation} \forall x\in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau}): \norm{p+(x,\phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}} ~-~ p}
    + \sigma < \sqrt{\sigma\tau} - \sigma
,\end{equation}
We wish to reiterate that $U_\textrm{ROI} = \{r_i ~|~ \norm{r - r_i}\leq \sqrt{\sigma \tau}\}$ and so $U_\textrm{ROI}\subset B_D(r, \sqrt{\sigma\tau})$.
Furthermore, since $\norm{r - p}\leq \sigma$, we have $B_D(p, \sqrt{\sigma\tau} - \sigma)\subset  B_D(r, \sqrt{\sigma\tau})$.
Accordingly, all points $p+(x, \phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ for  $x\in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2 \sqrt{\sigma\tau})$ are within our region of interest even when moved $\sigma$ away from the manifold in some direction into $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ (in Fig. \ref{fig:ManifoldGoodDisc_clean}  $B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau})$ is the orange disc and the projections of $p+(x, \phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}} + \varepsilon(x)$ onto $T_p\mathcal{M}$ are limited by the green disc containing the orange disc).
Using the calculations in Appendix \ref{subsec:simplification_app} we can use a simpler demand using $a_1$ and $a_2$, which ensures that the inequality \eqref{eq:a1a2_restriction_clean} is satisfied. The simplified requirement is
\begin{equation} (a_1+a_2)<\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} -\frac{\sqrt{2\sigma}}{\sqrt{\tau}}
.\end{equation}

Let us now bound the value of $\lrangle{\tilde q - p, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}^2$ from below, for any $\tilde  q\in \Gamma^\sigma_{\phi_p,B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau})}$.
Every such $\tilde  q$ can be written as
$
\tilde q = q + \varepsilon
$,
where $q\in \Gamma^0_{\phi_p,B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau})}$, and so 
 \begin{equation} (a_1 - a_2)\sqrt{\sigma\tau}  \leq \abs{q^x} \leq \|q^{\vec{x}}\| \leq \|p-x_0\|+a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau} = (a_1 + a_2)\sqrt{\sigma\tau}   
.\end{equation}
From Lemma \ref{lem:f_bound_circle_clean} we get that
\[
\abs{\lrangle{q, y_{\tilde j}}} \leq \tau-\sqrt{\tau^2-\norm{q^{\vec{x}}}^2} 
.\]
Thus, 
\[
\abs{\langle \tilde{q}, y_{\tilde j} \rangle} = |\tilde{q}^y| \leq \tau+\sigma-\sqrt{\tau^2-\|q^{\vec{x}}\|^2}
,\]
and by plugging the right hand side of \eqref{eq:qxBound_clean} we get
\begin{align*}
\langle \tilde{q}, y_{\tilde j} \rangle^2 & \leq \left(\tau+ \sigma -\sqrt{\tau^2-(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma\tau}\right)^2
 =\tau^2 \left(1+ \sigma/\tau -\sqrt{1-(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau}\right)^2
\\&\leq \tau^2(1+\sigma/\tau -(1-(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau))^2
= \tau^2 (\sigma/\tau +  (a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau)^2
\\&=  \sigma^2(1 +  (a_1+a_2)^2)^2
\leq 2\sigma^2
,\end{align*}
where the last inequality comes from \eqref{eq:a1a2_simplification_clean}.
Since $\angle(y_{\tilde j}, \tilde y_{\tilde j}) =\beta_{\tilde j} $ we can use the Euclidean geometry on $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$ (Figure \ref{fig:Lk_clean}) to get
\[
\lrangle{q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}} = \lrangle{q, \textrm{Rot}(\beta_{\tilde j}) y_{\tilde j}} = \lrangle{\textrm{Rot}(-\beta_{\tilde j}) q,  y_{\tilde j}}
,\]
where $\textrm{Rot}(\theta)$ denotes the rotation matrix in $\mathbb{R}^D$ with respect to the angle $\theta$ in $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$ .
Therefore,
$$|\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle| \geq \abs{-|q^x|\sin \beta_{\tilde j}  + |q^y|\cos \beta_{\tilde j}} = \abs{|q^x|\sin \beta_{\tilde j}  - |q^y|\cos \beta_{\tilde j}}.$$
Using Lemma \ref{lem:f_bound_circle_clean} and \eqref{eq:qxBound_clean} as before we get
\begin{align*}
 |\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle| &=\abs{  |q^x|\sin \beta_{\tilde j}  -  \left(\tau-\sqrt{\tau^2-\|q^{\vec{x}}\|^2} \right)\cos \beta_{\tilde j}}
 \\
 &\geq\left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma\tau}\sin \beta_{\tilde j}  -  \tau\left(1-\sqrt{1- (a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau} \right)\cos \beta_{\tilde j} \right)
 \\
 &\geq\tau\left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \beta_{\tilde j}-\cos \beta_{\tilde j} + \cos \beta_{\tilde j}(1- (a_1+a_2)^2\sigma /\tau) \right)
 \\
 &= \tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \beta_{\tilde j} -(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau \cos\beta_{\tilde j}\right)
 \\
 &\geq \tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \beta_{\tilde j} -(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau \right) 
,\end{align*}
and
\begin{equation} |\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle| \geq \tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0 -(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau \right) 
.\end{equation}
Since 
$\|\tilde{q} - q\| \leq \sigma $
we get 
$$\abs{\lrangle{\tilde q - q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}} = |\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle - \langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| \leq\sigma,$$
and so,
\begin{align*}
|\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| - |\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle|&\leq |\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle - \langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| \leq  \sigma\\
|\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle|&\geq |\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| - \sigma\\
\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle^2&\geq \langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle^2 - 2\sigma|\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| + \sigma^2\\
\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle^2&\geq \langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle^2 - 2\sigma|\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle|
.\end{align*}
 Substituting $\abs{\lrangle{q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}}$ with the bound from \eqref{eq:q_yk_prod_clean} we get
\begin{align*}
    \lrangle{\tilde q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}^2 & \geq \tau^2 \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0 -  (a_1+a_2)^2{\sigma/\tau}\right)^2 \\&~~~ - 2\sigma\tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0 -  (a_1+a_2)^2{\sigma/\tau}\right) \\
    &\geq \tau^2\left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0 -  {\sigma/\tau}\right)^2 - 2\sigma\tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0\right)\\
    &= \tau^2 \left((a_1-a_2)^2{\sigma/\tau}\sin^2 \alpha_0 - 2(a_1-a_2)(\sigma/\tau)^{3/2}\sin\alpha_0 + (\sigma/\tau)^2\right) \\&~~~ -2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}\sqrt{\tau} \sin \alpha_0 \\
    &\geq (a_1-a_2)^2{\sigma\tau}\sin^2 \alpha_0 - 2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2}\sin\alpha_0 + \sigma^2 -2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}{\tau}^{1/2} \\
    &= (a_1-a_2)^2{\sigma\tau}\sin^2 \alpha_0 - 2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2} + \sigma^2 -2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}{\tau}^{1/2} \\
    &= (a_1-a_2)^2{\sigma\tau}\sin^2 \alpha_0 - 4(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2} + \sigma^2 
\end{align*}
Thus, by choosing for example $a_1 = \frac{1}{4}$ and $a_2 = \frac{1}{8}$ we get
\begin{equation}
    \lrangle{\tilde q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}^2 \geq \frac{1}{64}\sigma \tau sin\alpha_0 - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2}
.\end{equation}
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Choose a disc of the tangent plane along $u_{\tilde j}$ whose noisy graph lies in the ROI, bound the graph height there, and rotate by $\beta_{\tilde j}$ to lower-bound the component along $\tilde y_{\tilde j}$. The key step is the rotation estimate $|\langle q,\tilde y\rangle|\ge|q^x|\sin\beta-|q^y|\cos\beta$.

nodes.name: Samples as graph points plus noise
nodes.statement:
As a result of Corollary \ref{cor:GraphOfFunctionTau_ROI}, $r_i \in U_\textrm{ROI}$ can be written as 
$$
r_i = \underbrace{p+(x_i, \phi_p(x_i))}_{p_i}+\varepsilon_i ,
$$
where $x_i=Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i - p)\in T_{p}\mathcal{M}$ and $\|\varepsilon_i\| \leq \sigma$.
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Write samples via Corollary 8.14.

nodes.name: Look for a good disc
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Seek $x_0,\rho$ such that the $\sigma$-thickened graph over the disc lies in the ROI.

nodes.name: Choice criterion
nodes.statement: Furthermore, we choose $x_0$ and $\rho$, such that $\lrangle{r_i - p, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}^2$ is large for any point $r_i\in\Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}^\sigma$ (see Figure \ref{fig:ManifoldGoodDisc_clean} for an illustration).
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Choose the disc where the normal component is large.

nodes.name: Coordinates and disc parameters
nodes.statement:
For convenience, we denote by $q^y, q^x, q^{\vec x}$ the projections of $q\in \Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}^\sigma$ onto $y_{\tilde j}$ (i.e., $T_p\mathcal{M}^\perp\cap \mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$), $u_{\tilde j}$ (i.e., $T_p\mathcal{M}\cap \mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$) and $T_p\mathcal{M}$ respectively.
Let $a_1, a_2<1$ and we define 
\[\rho = a_2 \cdot\sqrt{\sigma\tau}, ~~~\mbox{ and }~~~
x_0 = (a_1\sqrt{\sigma\tau})\cdot u_{\tilde j}\in T_p\mathcal{M} \cap \mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}.\]
That is, 
$
\norm{p - x_0} = a_1 \cdot \sqrt{\sigma\tau}
$.
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Introduce projections and set $\rho=a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau}$, $x_0=a_1\sqrt{\sigma\tau}u_{\tilde j}$.

nodes.name: Containment requirement
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Require the thickened graph over the disc to lie inside the ROI.

nodes.name: Containment discussion
nodes.statement:
We wish to reiterate that $U_\textrm{ROI} = \{r_i ~|~ \norm{r - r_i}\leq \sqrt{\sigma \tau}\}$ and so $U_\textrm{ROI}\subset B_D(r, \sqrt{\sigma\tau})$.
Furthermore, since $\norm{r - p}\leq \sigma$, we have $B_D(p, \sqrt{\sigma\tau} - \sigma)\subset  B_D(r, \sqrt{\sigma\tau})$.
Accordingly, all points $p+(x, \phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ for  $x\in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2 \sqrt{\sigma\tau})$ are within our region of interest even when moved $\sigma$ away from the manifold in some direction into $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ (in Fig. \ref{fig:ManifoldGoodDisc_clean}  $B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau})$ is the orange disc and the projections of $p+(x, \phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}} + \varepsilon(x)$ onto $T_p\mathcal{M}$ are limited by the green disc containing the orange disc).
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Explain why the requirement keeps points within the ROI.

nodes.name: Simplified requirement
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Replace the requirement by $(a_1+a_2)<1/\sqrt2-\sqrt{2\sigma/\tau}$.

nodes.name: Goal: lower bound
nodes.statement: Let us now bound the value of $\lrangle{\tilde q - p, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}^2$ from below, for any $\tilde  q\in \Gamma^\sigma_{\phi_p,B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau})}$.
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Aim to lower-bound $\langle\tilde q-p,\tilde y_{\tilde j}\rangle^2$.

nodes.name: Decompose tilde q
nodes.statement:
Every such $\tilde  q$ can be written as
$
\tilde q = q + \varepsilon
$,
where $q\in \Gamma^0_{\phi_p,B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau})}$, and so 
 \begin{equation} (a_1 - a_2)\sqrt{\sigma\tau}  \leq \abs{q^x} \leq \|q^{\vec{x}}\| \leq \|p-x_0\|+a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau} = (a_1 + a_2)\sqrt{\sigma\tau}   
.\end{equation}
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Write $\tilde q=q+\varepsilon$ and bound $|q^x|$.

nodes.name: Bound the y-component
nodes.statement:
From Lemma \ref{lem:f_bound_circle_clean} we get that
\[
\abs{\lrangle{q, y_{\tilde j}}} \leq \tau-\sqrt{\tau^2-\norm{q^{\vec{x}}}^2} 
.\]
Thus, 
\[
\abs{\langle \tilde{q}, y_{\tilde j} \rangle} = |\tilde{q}^y| \leq \tau+\sigma-\sqrt{\tau^2-\|q^{\vec{x}}\|^2}
,\]
and by plugging the right hand side of \eqref{eq:qxBound_clean} we get
\begin{align*}
\langle \tilde{q}, y_{\tilde j} \rangle^2 & \leq \left(\tau+ \sigma -\sqrt{\tau^2-(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma\tau}\right)^2
 =\tau^2 \left(1+ \sigma/\tau -\sqrt{1-(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau}\right)^2
\\&\leq \tau^2(1+\sigma/\tau -(1-(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau))^2
= \tau^2 (\sigma/\tau +  (a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau)^2
\\&=  \sigma^2(1 +  (a_1+a_2)^2)^2
\leq 2\sigma^2
,\end{align*}
where the last inequality comes from \eqref{eq:a1a2_simplification_clean}.
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 8.15 bounds the $y_{\tilde j}$ component by about $2\sigma^2$.

nodes.name: Rotate by beta
nodes.statement:
Since $\angle(y_{\tilde j}, \tilde y_{\tilde j}) =\beta_{\tilde j} $ we can use the Euclidean geometry on $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$ (Figure \ref{fig:Lk_clean}) to get
\[
\lrangle{q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}} = \lrangle{q, \textrm{Rot}(\beta_{\tilde j}) y_{\tilde j}} = \lrangle{\textrm{Rot}(-\beta_{\tilde j}) q,  y_{\tilde j}}
,\]
where $\textrm{Rot}(\theta)$ denotes the rotation matrix in $\mathbb{R}^D$ with respect to the angle $\theta$ in $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$ .
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Express $\langle q,\tilde y\rangle$ by a rotation in $\mathcal{L}_{\tilde j}$.

nodes.name: Rotation lower bound
nodes.statement:
Therefore,
$$|\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle| \geq \abs{-|q^x|\sin \beta_{\tilde j}  + |q^y|\cos \beta_{\tilde j}} = \abs{|q^x|\sin \beta_{\tilde j}  - |q^y|\cos \beta_{\tilde j}}.$$
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Lower bound by $|q^x|\sin\beta-|q^y|\cos\beta$.

nodes.name: Lower bound for clean points
nodes.statement:
Using Lemma \ref{lem:f_bound_circle_clean} and \eqref{eq:qxBound_clean} as before we get
\begin{align*}
 |\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle| &=\abs{  |q^x|\sin \beta_{\tilde j}  -  \left(\tau-\sqrt{\tau^2-\|q^{\vec{x}}\|^2} \right)\cos \beta_{\tilde j}}
 \\
 &\geq\left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma\tau}\sin \beta_{\tilde j}  -  \tau\left(1-\sqrt{1- (a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau} \right)\cos \beta_{\tilde j} \right)
 \\
 &\geq\tau\left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \beta_{\tilde j}-\cos \beta_{\tilde j} + \cos \beta_{\tilde j}(1- (a_1+a_2)^2\sigma /\tau) \right)
 \\
 &= \tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \beta_{\tilde j} -(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau \cos\beta_{\tilde j}\right)
 \\
 &\geq \tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \beta_{\tilde j} -(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau \right) 
,\end{align*}
and
\begin{equation} |\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle| \geq \tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0 -(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau \right) 
.\end{equation}
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Get the bound (60) for clean points $q$.

nodes.name: Account for the noise
nodes.statement:
Since 
$\|\tilde{q} - q\| \leq \sigma $
we get 
$$\abs{\lrangle{\tilde q - q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}} = |\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle - \langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| \leq\sigma,$$
and so,
\begin{align*}
|\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| - |\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle|&\leq |\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle - \langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| \leq  \sigma\\
|\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle|&\geq |\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| - \sigma\\
\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle^2&\geq \langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle^2 - 2\sigma|\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle| + \sigma^2\\
\langle \tilde{q}, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle^2&\geq \langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle^2 - 2\sigma|\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j}\rangle|
.\end{align*}
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Noise changes the component by at most $\sigma$.

nodes.name: Substitute
nodes.statement:
Substituting $\abs{\lrangle{q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}}$ with the bound from \eqref{eq:q_yk_prod_clean} we get
\begin{align*}
    \lrangle{\tilde q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}^2 & \geq \tau^2 \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0 -  (a_1+a_2)^2{\sigma/\tau}\right)^2 \\&~~~ - 2\sigma\tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0 -  (a_1+a_2)^2{\sigma/\tau}\right) \\
    &\geq \tau^2\left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0 -  {\sigma/\tau}\right)^2 - 2\sigma\tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0\right)\\
    &= \tau^2 \left((a_1-a_2)^2{\sigma/\tau}\sin^2 \alpha_0 - 2(a_1-a_2)(\sigma/\tau)^{3/2}\sin\alpha_0 + (\sigma/\tau)^2\right) \\&~~~ -2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}\sqrt{\tau} \sin \alpha_0 \\
    &\geq (a_1-a_2)^2{\sigma\tau}\sin^2 \alpha_0 - 2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2}\sin\alpha_0 + \sigma^2 -2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}{\tau}^{1/2} \\
    &= (a_1-a_2)^2{\sigma\tau}\sin^2 \alpha_0 - 2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2} + \sigma^2 -2(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}{\tau}^{1/2} \\
    &= (a_1-a_2)^2{\sigma\tau}\sin^2 \alpha_0 - 4(a_1-a_2)\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2} + \sigma^2 
\end{align*}
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.statement_short: Combine to a lower bound on the squared component.

nodes.name: Choose a_1, a_2
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2

nodes.name: sigma-thickened graph over a disc
nodes.statement:
\Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}^\sigma \stackrel{\bigtriangleup}{=} \{x ~|~ dist(x, \Gamma_{\phi_p, B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, \rho)}) < \sigma\}
,
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2

nodes.name: Containment requirement on a_1, a_2
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.label: eq:a1a2_restriction_clean

nodes.name: Simplified requirement on a_1, a_2
nodes.statement:
(a_1+a_2)<\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} -\frac{\sqrt{2\sigma}}{\sqrt{\tau}}
.
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.label: eq:a1a2_simplification_clean

nodes.name: Bounds on |q^x|
nodes.statement:
(a_1 - a_2)\sqrt{\sigma\tau}  \leq \abs{q^x} \leq \|q^{\vec{x}}\| \leq \|p-x_0\|+a_2\sqrt{\sigma\tau} = (a_1 + a_2)\sqrt{\sigma\tau}   
.
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.label: eq:qxBound_clean

nodes.name: Lower bound for clean points
nodes.statement:
|\langle q, \tilde{y}_{\tilde j} \rangle| \geq \tau \left((a_1-a_2)\sqrt{\sigma/\tau}\sin \alpha_0 -(a_1+a_2)^2\sigma/\tau \right) 
.
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2
nodes.label: eq:q_yk_prod_clean

nodes.name: Lower bound on squared normal component
nodes.statement:
\lrangle{\tilde q, \tilde y_{\tilde j}}^2 \geq \frac{1}{64}\sigma \tau sin\alpha_0 - \frac{1}{2}\sigma^{3/2}\tau^{1/2}
.
nodes.section: 9.2.3 Proof of Claim thm:claim_ri_tyk_bound_clean of Lemma 4.2

nodes.name: Simplification of the containment requirement
nodes.statement:
We wish to rewrite the requirement of \eqref{eq:a1a2_restriction_clean} in terms of $a_1$ and $a_2$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:f_bound_circle_clean}, for all $x\in B_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(x_0, a_2 \sqrt{\sigma\tau})$:
\begin{equation*}
    \|\phi_p(x)\| \leq \tau - \sqrt{\tau^2 - (a_1+a_2)^2 {\sigma\tau}} 
;\end{equation*}
see Figure \ref{fig:ManifoldGoodDisc_clean}.
Thus,
\begin{align*}
\norm{(x,\phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}}}
& \leq \sqrt{(a_1+a_2)^2 {\sigma\tau} + \left(\tau - \sqrt{\tau^2 - (a_1+a_2)^2 {\sigma\tau}}\right)^2} \\
&= \sqrt{(a_1+a_2)^2{\sigma\tau} + \tau^2 - 2\tau\sqrt{\tau^2 - (a_1+a_2)^2 {\sigma\tau}} + \tau^2 - (a_1+a_2)^2 {\sigma\tau}} \\
&= \sqrt{2\tau^2 - 2\tau^2\sqrt{1 - (a_1+a_2)^2 {\sigma/\tau}} } \\
&= \tau\sqrt{2} \sqrt{1 - \sqrt{1 - (a_1+a_2)^2 {\sigma/\tau}} } \\
&\leq \tau\sqrt{2} \sqrt{1 - (1 - (a_1+a_2)^2 {\sigma/\tau}) } \\
&= \sqrt{2}(a_1+a_2) \tau\sqrt{ {\sigma/\tau} } \\
&= \sqrt{2}(a_1+a_2) \sqrt{ {\sigma\tau} },\end{align*}
Where the second inequality results from applying \eqref{eq:Taylor2ndOrder}.
Therefore, the requirement of \eqref{eq:a1a2_restriction_clean} translates to
$$
\norm{(x,\phi_p(x))_{T_p\mathcal{M}}}_{T_p\mathcal{M},y_{\tilde j}}\leq \sqrt{2}(a_1+a_2)\sqrt{\sigma\tau}<\sqrt{\sigma\tau}-2\sigma
,$$
which can be simplified to 
$$
(a_1+a_2)<\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} - \frac{\sqrt{2\sigma}}{\sqrt{\tau}} 
.$$
nodes.statement_short: Bounding the graph norm over the disc via Lemma 8.15 and a Taylor bound shows that (58) suffices for (57).

nodes.name: Number of samples in a ball
nodes.statement:
Suppose $\nu$ is a distribution on $\Omega\subset B_d(0,R) \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ which is close to the uniform distribution $\mu$. That is, there exists $\mu_{max}$, $\mu_{min}$  such that for any $x\in \Omega$ we have  $\mu_{\min}\mu(x) \leq \nu(x) \leq \mu_{\max}\mu(x)$. Suppose $X=\{x_j\}_{j=1}^n$ is a set of $n$ i.i.d. sample from $\nu$, and denote the volume of a $ d $-dimensional unit ball by  $ \mathrm{V}_d = \frac{\pi^{d/2}}{\Gamma(d/2+1)} $. For any $\varepsilon$, $\delta$ and radius $\rho$, there is $N$, such that if $n>N$ the following holds: For any $x_0\in \Omega$ such that $B_d(x_0,\rho)\subset \Omega$, we have 
\[
n(\frac{\mu_{max}}{2}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d-\varepsilon) < \#|X \cap B_d(x_0, \rho)| < n(2\cdot \mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d+\varepsilon)
\]
with probability of at least $1-\delta$, where $\#|A|$ denotes the number of elements in the set $A$.
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
assumptions: Suppose $\nu$ is a distribution on $\Omega\subset B_d(0,R) \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ which is close to the uniform distribution $\mu$.
Suppose $X=\{x_j\}_{j=1}^n$ is a set of $n$ i.i.d. sample from $\nu$
conclusions: with probability of at least $1-\delta$, where $\#|A|$ denotes the number of elements in the set $A$.
nodes.statement_short: For a nearly uniform density, w.h.p. every ball of radius $\rho$ inside $\Omega$ contains between about $n\mu_{max}V_d\rho^d/2$ and $2n\mu_{min}V_d\rho^d$ samples.
nodes.label: lem:sampling_density_almost_uniform_clean

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.1
nodes.statement:
Since $\Omega \subset B_d(0,R)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, there exists an $\tilde\varepsilon$-net (denoted by $\Xi$) such that 
\[
\#\abs{\Xi} = \ceil{ \frac{3R}{\tilde\varepsilon}}^d
,\]
where $ \ceil{x} $ is the ceiling value of $ x $ \cite{vershynin2018high}.
Around each point $p$ in $\Xi$, we consider a ball $B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$. 
Note, that this $\tilde\varepsilon$-net along with these balls are independent of the choice of a specific ball $B_d(x_0,\rho)$.

For each of the $B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ , we  consider our sample set as $n$ i.i.d random variables   $Z^p_j$ which return the value $1$ if the sample lies within $B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ and $0$ if not.
Naturally, we get for all $j$ that
\[
\Pr[z_j^p = 1] = \int\limits_{B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)} d\nu 
\] 
Applying Hoeffding's inequality for each of the $B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ we arrive at
\begin{equation} \Pr[\overline{Z}^p - \mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] \leq -\varepsilon] \leq e^{-2 n \varepsilon^2}
,    
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation} \Pr[\overline{Z}^p - \mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] \geq \varepsilon] \leq e^{-2 n \varepsilon^2}
,    
\end{equation}
where
\[
\overline{Z}^p = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n Z_j^p.
\]
As a result
\[
\mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n\Pr[Z_j^p = 1] =
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n\int\limits_{B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)}d\nu
,\]
and
\begin{equation} \mu_{min} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)) \leq \mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] \leq \mu_{max} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho))
.\end{equation}
Plugging this into \eqref{eq:HoeffingtonInequality1_clean} we get
\begin{equation} \Pr\left[\overline{Z}^p - \mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}\left(B_d(p, (1- \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)\right)\leq -\varepsilon\right] \leq e^{-2n \varepsilon^2}
,\end{equation}
or, alternatively, since $\#|X \cap B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)| = n \cdot \overline{Z}^p$ we get
\[
\Pr\left[\#|X \cap B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)| \leq n(\mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))-\varepsilon)\right]\leq e^{-2n \varepsilon^2}
.\]

Denoting by $A_p$ the event $\#|X \cap B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)| \leq n(\mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))-\varepsilon)$ we use the union bound to achieve 
\begin{equation} \Pr\left(\bigcup\limits_{p\in\Xi} A_p\right) \leq \sum\limits_{p\in\Xi} \Pr\left(A_p \right) \leq \ceil{ 3R/\tilde\varepsilon}^d \cdot  e^{-2n \varepsilon^2}
.\end{equation}
Explicitly, the chances that there exists $B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ containing \textbf{less} sampled points than $n(\mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))-\varepsilon)$ are less than $c \cdot e^{-2n \varepsilon^2}$, where $c = \ceil{ 3R/\tilde\varepsilon}^d$.
Going back to $B_d(x_0, \rho)$, we know that there exists a point $\tilde p\in \Xi$ such that 
\[
B_d(\tilde p,(1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)\subset B_d(x_0, \rho)
.\]
As a result, for any $\delta, \varepsilon, \rho$ there exists $N$ such that for all $n>N$
\[
\#|X \cap B_d(x_0, \rho)| > n(\mu_{max}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d((1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))-\varepsilon)
= n(\mu_{max}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot(1-\tilde\varepsilon)^d\rho^d-\varepsilon)
,\]
with probability larger than $1-\delta$, where
\[
\mathrm{V}_d = \frac{\pi^{d/2}}{\Gamma(d/2+1)}
.\]

Similarly, instead of considering $B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ we look at $B_d(p, (1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ for $p\in\Xi$ and alter the definitions of $Z^p$ accordingly.
Then, by plugging the left inequality of \eqref{eq:EzBounds_clean} into \eqref{eq:HoeffingtonInequality2_clean} we get
\[
\Pr[\overline{Z}^p - \mu_{min}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d((1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))\geq \varepsilon] \leq e^{-2n\varepsilon^2} 
\]
Utilizing the union bound once more we get the same bound as in \eqref{eq:UnionBoundAp_clean}. 
In other words, the chances that there exists a $B_d(p, (1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ containing \textbf{more} sampled points than $n(\mu_{min} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(B_d((1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)) + \varepsilon )$ are less than $\ceil{3R/\tilde\varepsilon}^d\cdot e^{-2n\varepsilon^2}$.

Going back to $B_d(x_0, \rho)$, we know that there exists a point $\tilde p\in \Xi$ such that 
\[
B_d(x_0, \rho) \subset B_d(\tilde p,(1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)
,\]
and for $\tilde\varepsilon$ small enough
\[
B_d(\tilde p,(1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho) \subset \Omega
.\]
As a result, for any $\delta, \varepsilon, \rho$ there exists $N$ such that for all $n>N$
\[
\#|X \cap B_d(x_0, \rho)| < n(\mu_{min}\mathrm{Vol}(B_d((1+\tilde\varepsilon)\rho))+\varepsilon)
= n(\mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot(1+\tilde\varepsilon)^d\rho^d+\varepsilon)
,\]
with probability larger than $1-\delta$.

Finally, we get that for any $\delta, \varepsilon, \rho$ there exists $N$ large enough such that if $n>N$ we get
\[
n(\mu_{max}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot(1-\tilde\varepsilon)^d\rho^d-\varepsilon) < \#|X \cap B_d(x_0, \rho)| < n(\mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot(1+\tilde\varepsilon)^d\rho^d+\varepsilon)
\]
Since this is true for any $\tilde\varepsilon$, $(1+1/a)^a \leq 3$ and $(1-1/a)^a \geq 0.25$ we can choose $\tilde\varepsilon = \frac{1}{c_1 d}$ such that
\[(1 - \tilde\varepsilon)^d \geq 0.25^{1/c_1} \geq 0.5,\]
and
\[(1 + \tilde\varepsilon)^d \leq 3^{1/c_1} \leq 2,\]
and achieve
\[
n(\frac{\mu_{max}}{2}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d-\varepsilon) < \#|X \cap B_d(x_0, \rho)| < n(2\cdot \mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d+\varepsilon)
\]
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
nodes.statement_short: Cover by an $\tilde\varepsilon$-net, apply Hoeffding's inequality to slightly shrunken and enlarged balls around net points, and union-bound over the net.

nodes.name: Epsilon-net and balls
nodes.statement:
Since $\Omega \subset B_d(0,R)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$, there exists an $\tilde\varepsilon$-net (denoted by $\Xi$) such that 
\[
\#\abs{\Xi} = \ceil{ \frac{3R}{\tilde\varepsilon}}^d
,\]
where $ \ceil{x} $ is the ceiling value of $ x $ \cite{vershynin2018high}.
Around each point $p$ in $\Xi$, we consider a ball $B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$. 
Note, that this $\tilde\varepsilon$-net along with these balls are independent of the choice of a specific ball $B_d(x_0,\rho)$.
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
nodes.statement_short: Take an $\tilde\varepsilon$-net and shrunken balls around its points.

nodes.name: Indicator variables
nodes.statement:
For each of the $B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ , we  consider our sample set as $n$ i.i.d random variables   $Z^p_j$ which return the value $1$ if the sample lies within $B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)$ and $0$ if not.
Naturally, we get for all $j$ that
\[
\Pr[z_j^p = 1] = \int\limits_{B_d(p, (1-\tilde\varepsilon)\rho)} d\nu 
\]

nodes.statement_short: Define indicators of samples in each ball.

nodes.name: Hoeffding
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
nodes.statement_short: Apply Hoeffding's inequality in both directions.

nodes.name: Expectation bounds
nodes.statement:
As a result
\[
\mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n\Pr[Z_j^p = 1] =
\frac{1}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n\int\limits_{B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)}d\nu
,\]
and
\begin{equation} \mu_{min} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho)) \leq \mathbb{E}[\overline{Z}^p] \leq \mu_{max} \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(B_d(p, (1 - \tilde\varepsilon)\rho))
.\end{equation}

As a result, for any $\delta, \varepsilon, \rho$ there exists $N$ such that for all $n>N$

,\]
with probability larger than $1-\delta$, where
\[

.\]

nodes.name: The projection of the Lebesgue measure onto T_pM is almost uniform
nodes.statement:
Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with bounded reach $\tau$ and a Riemannian metric $G$ pronounced through the chart $\varphi_p$ around a point $ p\in \mathcal{M} $ \eqref{eq:LocalChart_clean}. 
    Let $r\in\mathcal{M}_\sigma$, and let $\mu, \mu_{\mathcal{M}}, \mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ denote the uniform distribution on $\mathcal{M}_\sigma\subset\mathbb{R}^D$, $\mathcal{M}$, $T_p\mathcal{M}$ correspondingly.
    Denote $Proj_{\mathcal{M}}, Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ the projection operators onto $\mathcal{M}$ and $T_p\mathcal{M}$.
    Then $\left(Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}Proj_{\mathcal{M}}\right)_*\mu$ is a measure on $T_p\mathcal{M}$, and upon restricting this measure to $B_d(0,\rho)$ for some $\rho < \tau/2$ we get
    \[
    (Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}Proj_{\mathcal{M}})_*\mu = \mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d} \sqrt{det(G)}\mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}
    ,\]
    where $\mathrm{V}_d$ denotes the volume of a $d$-dimensional ball.
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with bounded reach $\tau$ and a Riemannian metric $G$ pronounced through the chart $\varphi_p$ around a point $ p\in \mathcal{M} $ \eqref{eq:LocalChart_clean}.
nodes.label: lem:measure_projecting_to_tangent_clean

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.2
nodes.statement:
We first note that since $\mu$ is the Lebesgue measure on $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ we have
\[
\int_{\mathcal{M}_\sigma} d\mu = \int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d}\mu_{\mathcal{M}}
,\]
where $\mu_{\mathcal{M}}$ is the uniform distribution on $\mathcal{M}$. Thus,
\[
Proj_{\mathcal{M}} \mu = {\mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d}}\mu_{\mathcal{M}}
.\]
Now, $Proj_{\mathcal{M}}\mu$ is a measure defined on $\mathcal{M}$, which can be pulled back to the tangent domain $T_p\mathcal{M}\simeq\mathbb{R}^d$ in the neighborhood $B_d(p, \tau/2)$ according to Corollary \ref{cor:GraphOfFunctionTau2_clean}.
If we denote the chart from $T_p\mathcal{M}\simeq\mathbb{R}^d$ to $\mathcal{M}$ by $\varphi_p$ we get
\[
(Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}Proj_{\mathcal{M}})_*\mu = \mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d} \sqrt{det(G)}\mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}
,\]
where $G$ is the Riemannian metric expressed in this chart, and $\mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ is the Lebesgue measure on $T_p\mathcal{M}$.
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
nodes.statement_short: Push the uniform measure on the tube forward to the manifold, then pull back through the chart, picking up $\sqrt{\det G}$.

nodes.name: Push forward to M
nodes.statement:
We first note that since $\mu$ is the Lebesgue measure on $\mathcal{M}_\sigma$ we have
\[
\int_{\mathcal{M}_\sigma} d\mu = \int_{\mathcal{M}}\mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d}\mu_{\mathcal{M}}
,\]
where $\mu_{\mathcal{M}}$ is the uniform distribution on $\mathcal{M}$. Thus,
\[
Proj_{\mathcal{M}} \mu = {\mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d}}\mu_{\mathcal{M}}
.\]
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
nodes.statement_short: The tube measure projects to a multiple of the uniform measure on $\mathcal{M}$.

nodes.name: Pull back through the chart
nodes.statement:
Now, $Proj_{\mathcal{M}}\mu$ is a measure defined on $\mathcal{M}$, which can be pulled back to the tangent domain $T_p\mathcal{M}\simeq\mathbb{R}^d$ in the neighborhood $B_d(p, \tau/2)$ according to Corollary \ref{cor:GraphOfFunctionTau2_clean}.
If we denote the chart from $T_p\mathcal{M}\simeq\mathbb{R}^d$ to $\mathcal{M}$ by $\varphi_p$ we get
\[
(Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}Proj_{\mathcal{M}})_*\mu = \mathrm{V}_{D-d}\sigma^{D-d} \sqrt{det(G)}\mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}
,\]
where $G$ is the Riemannian metric expressed in this chart, and $\mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ is the Lebesgue measure on $T_p\mathcal{M}$.
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
nodes.statement_short: Pull back to the tangent plane via Corollary 8.13.

nodes.name: Density bounds for the projected measure
nodes.statement:
From the fact that $\mathcal{M}\in\mathcal{C}^k$ is compact and the restriction to a ball of radius $\tau/2$ we get that $\sqrt{det(G)}$ is bounded and
	\[
	\mu_{min} \mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}} \leq (Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}Proj_{\mathcal{M}})_*\mu \leq \mu_{max} \mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}
	\]
	where $\mu_{min}, \mu_{max}$ are constants that depend on $\tau$, and $\mu_{T_p\mathcal{M}}$ is the Lebesgue measure on $T_p\mathcal{M}$.
	The constants $ \mu_{min}, \mu_{max} $ can be described explicitly to show their exact relationship to $ \tau $.
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
nodes.label: cor:measure_projecting_bounds_clean

nodes.name: Number of samples projecting into a tangent ball
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
assumptions: Let $\mathcal{M}$ be a compact $d$-dimensional sub-manifold of $\mathbb{R}^D$ with reach $\tau$  bounded away from zero
assume $\sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} < \frac{1}{2}$.
Suppose that $\mu$ is the uniform distribution on $ \mathcal{M}_\sigma $.
nodes.statement_short: W.h.p. the number of samples projecting into a tangent-plane ball of radius $\rho$ is at most $\approx2n\mu_{min}V_d\rho^d$, and into radius $\rho+\sigma$ at least $\approx n\mu_{max}V\rho^d/2$.

nodes.name: mu_min and mu_max
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
nodes.label: eq:mu_min_max_def

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 9.4
nodes.statement:
Note that both the minimum and maximum in \eqref{eq:mu_min_max_def} exist and finite since $ \mathcal{M} $ is compact and the determinant is continuous.
	We mention that since $ \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} < \frac{1}{2} $ we get that $ \sqrt{\sigma \tau} < \frac{\tau}{2} $ and the conditions of Corollary \ref{cor:measure_projecting_bounds_clean} are met.
	Note that 
	\[
	\#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho) \} \leq \#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}\circ Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho) \}
	,\]
	and from Lemma \ref{lem:sampling_density_almost_uniform_clean} combined with Corollary \ref{cor:measure_projecting_bounds_clean} we get
	\[
	\#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}\circ Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho) \} \leq n(2\cdot \mu_{min}\cdot \mathrm{V}_d \cdot\rho^d+\varepsilon)
	.\]
	Thus, the first inequality is achieved.
	
	On the other hand,
	\[
	\#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho+\sigma) \}
	\geq \#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}\circ Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho)\}
	.\]
	Using again Lemma \ref{lem:sampling_density_almost_uniform_clean} combined with Corollary \ref{cor:measure_projecting_bounds_clean} we get
	\[
	\#\{r_i|Proj_{T_p\mathcal{M}}\circ Proj_{\mathcal{M}}(r_i) \in B_d(x_0,\rho)\} \geq n \left(\frac{\mu_{max}}{2}\cdot \mathrm{V}_{d} \cdot \rho^d - \varepsilon\right)
	,\]
	and the second inequality holds.
nodes.section: 9.3 Supporting Lemmas on Sample size in a given volume
nodes.statement_short: Compare tangent projections with projections through the manifold and apply Lemma 9.1 with Corollary 9.3.

nodes.name: Constants well defined
nodes.statement:
Note that both the minimum and maximum in \eqref{eq:mu_min_max_def} exist and finite since $ \mathcal{M} $ is compact and the determinant is continuous.
	We mention that since $ \sqrt{\frac{\sigma}{\tau}} < \frac{1}{2} $ we get that $ \sqrt{\sigma \tau} < \frac{\tau}{2} $ and the conditions of Corollary \ref{cor:measure_projecting_bounds_clean} are met.
